description: Codified the bypass-rationalization anti-pattern catalog closing the --no-verify commit loophole. Slice ships: (a) new KB doc cataloguing the 5 typical rationalizations (commit-only-harmless · I'm-fixing-the-tool · false-positive · no-impact · surface-after) each refuted on the methodology contract; (b) the canonical ea7514e7 worked example with full failure-mode walkthrough + 3 valid tech-lead resolution paths the agent should have surfaced for; (c) inline §2.6 surface protocol (STOP → SURFACE kind="surface" → RETURN-blocked → WAIT) since the broader bg-engineer-safety-discipline parent is in flight on a parallel branch and not yet on dev; (d) engineer-seed.md §9 Bash safety tightened with explicit dual coverage (commit AND push) + 5 rationalizations in a "Do not rationalize" subsection; (e) dispatch-engineer-tuning.md §4b mandatory brief language ("NEVER use --no-verify (commit OR push). NEVER --force. If a hook fails or any safety gate refuses, STOP and surface as a surface-note (kind='surface'); return blocked. target: products/social-wiring YT-OAuth multi-account flow — router calls non-existent GoogleProvider interface (PRODUCTION BUG masked by mocked tests)
description: REAL PRODUCTION BUG (severity high) found while investigating the cluster-C no-self-monkeypatch flag. products/social-wiring/backend/app/routers/integration_accounts_router.py imports the SEED GoogleProvider (from noctusai_lib.security.oauth) and calls `provider.get_auth_url(state=...)` (expecting a (url, verifier) tuple, sync) at youtube_oauth_start, and sync `provider.exchange_code(code=, code_verifier=)` expecting a DICT (bundle.get('access_token')) at youtube_oauth_callback. But the real seed GoogleProvider has NO get_auth_url anywhere in noctusai_lib (it exposes `async authorization_url`) and `exchange_code` is ASYNC returning a TokenSet, not a dict. ⇒ the multi-account YouTube OAuth flow would AttributeError on the first call in production; it has likely NEVER worked. The bug is INVISIBLE because tests/routers/test_integration_account_router.py monkeypatches GoogleProvider/_yt_pkce_redis_client/make_youtube_client with MagicMocks (16 sites) — the mocks satisfy any method/return, so the tests are GREEN while production is broken. Likely history: the seed OAuth was refactored to the canonical async Protocol+Fake (authorization_url/async exchange_code/TokenSet) and social-wiring's consumer was never migrated; the mocked tests masked the break. PROPER FIX (a real product slice, NOT a baseline-accept and NOT a quick inline test edit): (1) migrate the router to the real async GoogleProvider interface (authorization_url + async exchange_code→TokenSet, adapt token-bundle handling) — or add a DI seam + a correct adapter; (2) rewrite the test to inject the seed FakeOAuthProvider + make_youtube_client(use_fake=True) + a fake redis via dependency_overrides so it exercises the REAL interface and would catch this class of bug; (3) VERIFY the YT-OAuth flow actually works end-to-end. Surfaced + paused inline per the rabbit-hole/estimate-off-evidence discipline — recommend a dedicated focused fix (dispatch or next session), not a rushed end-of-marathon-session production-OAuth change.

DEPLOY-FLOW GAP: after deploy_image recreates a product container, cloudflared (noctus-tunnel) can keep a STALE origin connection to the pre-recreate container → that hostname returns edge-timeout (curl 000; CF connects+TLS+HTTP2 ok then hangs, 524-class) even though the new container is healthy + has the right docker-net alias. Observed 2026-06-01: after deploy_image social-wiring (+ core), core/apex routed fine but social.noctusai.com + social-wiring.noctusai.com both timed out at the edge; container healthy internally (/api/clients=401 new code live), alias 'social-wiring' present on noctus-net. Fix: `docker restart noctus-tunnel` re-resolved all origins → social 200 instantly. ROUND FIX: deploy_image should, after a recreate, signal cloudflared to re-resolve the affected origin (restart noctus-tunnel, or send SIGHUP, or the tunnel config should set originRequest keepAlive/connectTimeout low enough to drop dead origins fast). Add a post-recreate edge-reachability check (curl the public hostname with browser UA) to the deploy so this is caught automatically, not by manual smoke. Diagnosis tell: container healthy + internal curl OK + alias present + curl -v reaches CF edge+TLS but hangs with no origin response.

branch_pointer integration friction hit 2026-06-02 (orphan-branch leftover-claim caused a 5-step loop). THREE sub-drifts: (1) action=append did NOT auto-fill `session` from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID — the MCP server process env lacked the var, so the appended pointer carried null session → pre-push branch-tree mirror keeper HARD-BLOCKED the dev push ('null/empty session'). Workaround: pass session= explicitly (got it via echo $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in a shell). Fix: funnel-self-satisfy — branch_pointer should resolve session from the shell/git config when the env var is absent, or fail LOUDLY at append time (not silently write a null that only blocks at push). (2) action=append/update with push_dev=True COMMITS the pointer onto the CURRENT branch (HEAD), not onto dev — when HEAD is a feature/leftover branch this advances the branch tip PAST the pointer's recorded `commit`, which then trips the 'shipped but branch ahead of recorded commit' mirror check, and the auto FF-push to dev fails repeatedly ('FF-push to dev failed after retry'). The pointer ledger commit belongs on dev regardless of current HEAD. Workaround that worked: finish the code merge, checkout dev, delete the branch, THEN append the shipped pointer from dev. (3) push_dev=False writes the ledger to the working tree but does NOT commit, leaving uncommitted churn the caller must reconcile (sibling of the auto_ledger_appends_strand_on_primary class). Net: registering a leftover/orphan branch in the live map at integration time is far harder than it should be. ROUND FIX: a dedicated 'integrate-from-dev' pointer path that always commits on dev FF-only + auto-resolves session, mirroring task_branch's salvage-ledger discipline.

INLINE-SELF-BRANCH ENV-WIRING DRIFT (2026-06-02): self-branched for a noc methodology/docs task with raw `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/dev` instead of `noctus.dev.task_branch action=start`. A raw `git worktree` creates NO venv and does NO env-wiring, so the worktree's `mcp/noctusai/cli.py` self-exec finds no `mcp/noctusai/.venv` and falls back to system python → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'noctusai_lib'` on any ad-hoc `python cli.py --<gate>` run in the worktree. (The pre-commit HOOK itself is already worktree-safe — it resolves the MAIN repo's `venv/` via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and passes `--worktree-path` — so the commit still succeeded; only ad-hoc tooling broke.) ROUND FIX / rule: for an inline self-branch where you will run noc tooling, prefer `noctus.dev.task_branch action=start` (wires env: python + node_modules/@noctusai symlinks) OR, when a raw worktree is used, run gates via the MAIN repo venv exactly as the hook does: `<main-repo>/venv/bin/python <worktree>/mcp/noctusai/cli.py --<flag> --worktree-path <worktree>`. Never bare `python cli.py` inside a raw `git worktree`. Codification target: noc-self-branch skill + KB self-branching-mode (add the 'raw-worktree-has-no-venv → use task_branch or main-venv+--worktree-path' note). Sibling of feedback_cross_product_tsc_cleanup_learnings (task_branch wire_env / dangling-symlink class).

8-WAY-SYNC EMBED-MOVES-WITH-DOC BLOCKS WORKTREE KB EDITS (2026-06-02): editing an EXISTING KB doc and committing fails `check_eight_way_sync` ("8-way sync FAILED, Commit aborted") because that doc's kb-embeddings are stale (cached.sha ≠ live). NEW KB files do NOT block (no prior cached sha). Inconsistency: the pre-commit AUTO-REFRESHES structural caches (agent-context, noc-graph via settle_structural_caches, zero-OpenAI) but does NOT auto-refresh EMBEDDING caches — yet the 8-way-sync gate BLOCKS on stale kb-embeddings for STAGED kb docs while only WARNING on unrelated code/corpus/memory embedding staleness. So the gate blocks on a thing it won't auto-fix, and the two-tier-by-cost cadence (embeddings=warn-only) is contradicted for staged kb docs specifically. WORKAROUND used: `<main-repo>/venv/bin/python <worktree>/mcp/noctusai/cli.py --refresh-kb-embeddings --worktree-path <worktree>` (embeds worktree content → cache fresh vs worktree → commit passes). ROUND FIX options: (a) pre-commit auto-refreshes kb-embeddings for STAGED kb docs only (small, bounded OpenAI cost, like structural caches but embed) before the 8-way gate; OR (b) make the staged-kb-doc embedding check warn-only too (consistent two-tier-by-cost), deferring embed to push-time refresh. Hits any worktree KB-doc EDIT (recurring this session). Sibling of feedback_inline_self_branch_env_wiring (worktree tooling friction) + push-time-embedding-gate.

ABSORPTION TRACKING SHOULD BE A DERIVED NDJSON SYSTEM, NOT HAND-MAINTAINED INDEX ROWS (user flag 2026-06-02). Absorptions are now N=2 (social-wiring 2026-05-16 + orbity) — a recurring multi-session event. Hand-adding a KB INDEX 'By topic' catalog row per absorbed set is exactly the drift-prone pattern the absorb guide's own Gate 2 warns against ('derive any index from the manifest dir; never hand-maintain a parallel count'). Formalize an event-shaped tracking ledger `project-history/absorptions.ndjson` + `noctus.dev.absorption_*` MCP tools (status/append/query) mirroring branch-tree.ndjson + gen_promotions_index, tracking each absorption's lifecycle (source-cloned → diagnosed → capability-uplift-per-organ → pilot-validated → fleet-propagated → native-doc-landed → source-archived) AND per-capability uplift state (capability → target seed organ → pilot status → native-doc → de-referenced). EXTEND-BEFORE-SPAWN considerations: (a) gen_promotions_index already derives promotion-manifest items for the SIBLING-WORKSPACE absorption flavor — the FOREIGN-PLATFORM capability-uplift shape is the uncovered gap; (b) the orbity uplift is itself a multi-session initiative = roadmap territory (project-history/roadmaps/<slug>-YYYY-MM.md, durable+mutable for slice-state), while the ndjson is event-shaped — pick the right tier. The tracker earns its keep when the uplift DEV starts (right now: 1 absorption, 0 organs built → nothing to track yet). Composes: branch-tree-tracking + roadmap-tracking + gen_promotions_index + MCP-first-scripts + recurrence-formalize. Decision pending: build-now vs roadmap-now+defer-system vs extend-existing.

CORRECTION of the earlier 2026-06-02 entry "8-WAY-SYNC EMBED-MOVES-WITH-DOC BLOCKS WORKTREE KB EDITS" — that was a MISDIAGNOSIS. Empirically verified (2026-06-03): editing a KB file, staging it, and running the EXACT hook gate `--check-eight-way-sync --worktree-path <wt>` exits **0** — embedding-cache staleness (kb/code/corpus/memory) is severity=`warning` and the cli exit logic is `sys.exit(1 if any_high else 0)`, so embeddings NEVER block a commit (the pre-push hook batch-refreshes them — push-time-embedding-gate v4.1). The commit aborts I attributed to embeddings were actually the `[high]`-severity sub-keepers (check_agent_kb_alignment: a new PATTERNS/ doc unclaimed by any owns_kb/allowlist; check_claude_md_router word-cap) which my grep filters hid from view — and I then over-refreshed embeddings needlessly (wasted OpenAI cost + time). REAL lesson: (1) embedding staleness is warn-only — NEVER manually `--refresh-*` to "unblock" a commit; (2) when a commit aborts on 8-way-sync, the blocker is the `[high]` issue — grep/read for `[high]`, not the warning noise. ROUND FIX SHIPPED (same 2026-06-03 commit `0ddc331f`): cli.py `--check-eight-way-sync` now prints an explicit `✗ BLOCKED by N high-severity issue(s): <symbols>` line + a `(M advisory warning(s) — NOT blocking; embeddings refresh at push, don't manually refresh)` line, so the blocking-vs-advisory split is unmistakable and the misattribution cannot recur. Supersedes the earlier (wrong) entry; no further code change needed on the embed axis.

task_branch action=cleanup commits the worktree-salvage recovery pointer ONTO the feature branch being torn down (the branch tip ends up touching project-history/worktree-salvage.ndjson), then step 4 deletes that branch. For a branch integrated via REBASE (the common case — `git -C <wt> rebase origin/dev && push HEAD:dev`), `git branch -d` refuses (pre-rebase SHAs aren't dev ancestors) so the operator must `git branch -D`, which discards the salvage-pointer commit. Net: the salvage ledger never receives a row for rebase-integrated slugs (verified 2026-06-30: grep of worktree-salvage.ndjson for two just-cleaned slugs = 0 hits). Recovery value was nil this time (work fully on prod), but the ledger is silently incomplete. Root fix: cleanup should append+commit the salvage pointer to the PRIMARY's dev checkout (FF-push to dev, like branch_pointer/auto_improvement ledgers), NOT onto the branch it is about to delete. Same family as feedback_auto_ledger_appends_strand_on_primary.

The post-checkout (cache-refresh) hook appends a memory-embeddings cost row to project-history/vector-costs.ndjson during a `git rebase`'s base-checkout step, dirtying the working tree mid-rebase so git aborts with `cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes` and leaves a detached HEAD + stale .git/worktrees/<slug>/rebase-merge dir (hit twice 2026-06-30 doing worktree-explicit integrate). Workaround that worked: run fetch/checkout/rebase with `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` (cache-refresh is not a gate), `git restore` the churn, push WITH hooks (the real verification gate, never bypassed). Root-fix candidates: (a) post-checkout should NOT write the cost ledger during a rebase/cherry-pick sequence (detect GIT_REFLOG_ACTION / rebase-in-progress and skip), or (b) the embed-refresh should not append a cost row when nothing actually re-embedded (source_sha-guarded no-op should be cost-free). Sibling of feedback_vector_costs_ledger_auto_commit + the stale-primary-dev class just fixed (7767).

N=2 of the same idiom: `branch_pointer._ff_or_rebase_push_to_dev` (2026-06-30) + `task_branch._push_salvage_ledger_from_primary` (2026-06-30) both implement 'commit a project-history/*.ndjson ledger row on the primary dev checkout → fetch → divergence-guard → rebase-onto-origin/dev (union-merge, conflict-free) → FF-push, best-effort, single race-retry'. At N=3 (the next ledger needing dev-FF-push: e.g. absorptions.ndjson / worktree-salvage already done / a future cost-log push) MUST lift to ONE shared helper in tools/noctus/dev (or noctusai_lib) taking (runner, root, rel_ledger, dev_branch, remote). Surfaced by backend-engineer during the cleanup-salvage fix. DRY recurrence-rule: N=2 triage→accept, N=3 formalize.

Git hooks are wired via core.hooksPath → the MAIN repo's .git/hooks → symlinks into the MAIN working-tree's scripts/hooks/*. So a hook edit made IN a worktree is NOT exercised by a plain git command run from that worktree — git runs the MAIN tree's copy → false-green 'my hook fix works' (the harness-self-invisible-during-refactor shape). Workaround (used to verify the post-checkout fix 2026-06-30): exercise the worktree's hook copy via a per-invocation `git -c core.hooksPath=<worktree>/scripts/hooks ...` override. Codification target: a one-line note in KB § PATTERNS/common/cache-auto-freshness.md (hook-testing) so the next hook-editor doesn't get a false-green from running the unfixed MAIN copy. Surfaced by devops-engineer during the post-checkout rebase-skip fix.

deploy-prod.yml's SSH step runs `ssh-keyscan -H "$VPS_HOST" >> known_hosts 2>/dev/null` under `bash -e`; on a TRANSIENT VPS-unreachable blip ssh-keyscan returns no key (or nonzero) and `set -e` aborts the whole step with exit 1 and NO message (observed 2026-06-30: a dry-run failed pre-`echo`, a re-run immediately succeeded). The deploy itself is fine — it's a flaky-edge false-negative. Root-fix candidates: (a) retry ssh-keyscan a few times with backoff before failing; (b) `ssh-keyscan ... || { echo '::warning::host-key scan failed (transient?) — retrying'; sleep N; ssh-keyscan ...; }`; (c) pre-seed a pinned known_hosts entry as a repo secret so the runner never depends on a live scan. Low severity (re-run clears it) but worth hardening — same transient-edge class the client-side _vps_ssh throttle addresses for our local tools. Sibling of feedback_vps_ssh_throttle_circuit_breaker.

createProductLayout has NO cookie-session override seam — a half-shipped seed blocking erp-httponly-cookie-session Slice 3. It hard-binds Supabase-JS for logout (auth.signOut), password change (auth.updateUser), session-extend (auth.refreshSession) and page-status nav gating (.from() RLS read); ProductLayoutConfig.supabase is non-optional and LayoutEnrichment exposes only onUpdateProfile — no onLogout/onUpdatePassword/onExtend/page-status hatch. Consequence if ignored: swapping a product's AuthProvider to cookie-mode makes the header "Sair" a SILENT NO-OP (signOut against a never-established session; cookie never cleared) while still redirecting to /login — a false-appears-logged-out state, i.e. the migration's own goal #2 (logout reliability) regressed BY the migration. This is a THIRD half-shipped dimension of the cookie-session seed, FE-side, not previously logged (the roadmap tracks two BE-side: router-lived-in-fork + SessionStore Protocol+Fake-only). Also: social-wiring is cited in 03-SEED-ARCHITECTURE as the "first consumer" of createSessionAuthProvider, but its App.tsx still passes legacy {supabase,useAuthStore} to BOTH createProductLayout and createProductApp — only Login.tsx calls loginWithSession(). That is a login-only bolt-on, so the "first consumer" precedent does NOT prove the pattern works end-to-end. Fix shape: an authProvider-analogous escape hatch (or a sibling createSessionProductLayout) — cross-product, seed/architect layer, prerequisite slice before Slice 3 can re-dispatch.

description: cwd-reset hazard RECURRED and this time silently wrote to dev. Engineer C's Edit tool calls reported SUCCESS but did not land on its worktree disk — they resolved against the PRIMARY checkout (sitting on dev) instead. Two compounding harms: (1) the primary tree on dev was mutated by a dispatched engineer, violating the absolute never-work-on-dev rule; (2) the resulting unstaged residue in the primary tree BLOCKED the branch_pointer ledger push for BOTH the engineer and the tech-lead, because the pointer push path rebases against origin/dev inside the primary checkout — so one cwd-reset silently jammed the coordination ledger for the whole wave. Existing memory feedback_harness_cwd_resets_to_primary documents the hazard; this recurrence proves detection-by-discipline is insufficient. The engineer's own mitigation worked and is worth codifying: after every Edit, re-verify on-disk via git -C <worktree> status / diff --cached + literal grep, and re-author via python3 against an absolute worktree path when Edit lies. Proposed s4 keeper: a pre-Edit assertion refusing any write whose resolved path does not start with the declared worktree root. Tech-lead note: `git diff` alone is a FALSE-NEGATIVE detector here — it shows only UNSTAGED changes, so a staged engineer worktree reads as "empty" and looks like divergence; compare with `git diff --cached` (this misled the tech-lead mid-incident until corrected).

description: noctus.dev.register_organ and find_reusable_component lack the worktree_path parameter that most other noctus.dev.* tools carry. REPO_ROOT in mcp/noctusai/settings.py is a static constant resolved to the MCP server's startup workspace (the primary checkout), so these tools structurally CANNOT see files that exist only in a dispatched engineer's worktree. Consequence: the organ-registration leg of any worktree-isolated dispatch can never complete in-dispatch — it always returns bundle-not-found and forces a post-merge re-run by the tech-lead. Confirmed live this session: engineer D's register_organ("KanbanBoard") returned bundle-not-found from its worktree; the identical call succeeded from the primary tree once the branch was integrated and the tree fast-forwarded. description: PROD-PIN HOLE: the prod branch pin does NOT protect what actually runs. build-and-push.yml triggers on push to MAIN (paths products/**, seed/**) and moves :latest. The deploy model is GHCR-pull, so the running artifact comes from main — while release stage=promote pins the PROD BRANCH. Net effect: pinning prod to a safe sha (2f35bb74) still leaves :latest built from the main tip, which on 2026-07-16 contained 9be41bc2 (make_session_store refuses without SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY, absent in prod env) — a deploy_image --source pull :latest would have taken social-wiring down. Workaround used: gh workflow run build-and-push.yml --ref prod -f products=social-wiring, then deploy a pinned :<sha>. Fix options: build on prod pushes too, tag main builds as :edge instead of moving :latest, or make deploy_image refuse a :latest whose source sha is not an ancestor of origin/prod.

description: wire_env=True CONTAMINATES THE PRIMARY checkout's node_modules. It symlinks <worktree>/products/<slug>/frontend/node_modules -> PRIMARY's node_modules dir, then creates @noctusai/{lib,seed} INSIDE it — so that second link is written THROUGH the symlink into the PRIMARY, re-pointing every product's @noctusai/lib+seed at the worktree's seed copy. Last wire_env wins fleet-wide. Observed 2026-07-16: all 9 products in the primary resolved @noctusai/lib -> .claude/worktrees/n8n-page-ui/seed/lib/frontend (a peer's live worktree). Consequences: (a) the primary/dev-fleet builds against a PEER's seed, (b) inside a container the target is a /Users/... host path that does not exist, (c) repairing it would break the peer whose worktree is the current target — so it cannot be safely fixed while peers are live. Fix: create the @noctusai links against the worktree's REAL node_modules dir (resolve the symlink first / use a per-worktree node_modules), never through the shared symlink.
resolve_when: task_branch wire_env no longer mutates the primary checkout's node_modules (verified: primary @noctusai/lib points at primary seed after a worktree wire_env + cleanup)

description: PATTERN CANDIDATE — a scoped id held in ONE global slot leaks across scopes, and a reconcile effect cannot fix it. social-wiring's useActiveAccountStore held a single provider-agnostic activeAccountId read raw by every provider-scoped hook (youtube/meta/n8n/whatsapp); navigating between two provider pages sent the wrong provider's integration_accounts.id to a provider-scoped endpoint, producing a live 404 on /api/n8n/workflows (2026-07-31). Three parts worth generalizing. (1) The identifier's TYPE was narrower than its STORAGE: an account id is only meaningful to its provider, so a single-slot store is a type error the type system cannot see. (2) The team had already noticed and mitigated with a reconcile effect in ConnectedAccountSwitcher — but that effect runs only after the accounts query resolves while the data hooks fire on the same render, so it structurally loses the race. A post-hoc reconcile is evidence the state shape is wrong, not a fix. (3) The migration lever: REMOVING the flat field rather than deprecating it turned all 26 read sites into compile errors and surfaced three further leaking surfaces that no one had reported yet. Candidate keeper: flag a store field whose value is a scoped/foreign key when N distinct call sites read it under different scope literals. Sibling of the existing lying-loading-state and status-pagina-role-parity patterns — all three are 'the UI is confidently wrong rather than loudly broken'.
resolve_when: A second instance of the same shape appears (a single-slot store holding a scope-qualified id consumed by 2+ scoped surfaces) — at N=2 triage per the recurrence rule, N=3 MUST formalize to KB + keeper.

Two consequences: (1) it structurally cannot apply a migration authored in an engineer worktree — the file is invisible to it; (2) worse, a naive confirm=true issued FROM a worktree silently applies whatever is pending in the PRIMARY tree, i.e. other people's unvetted migrations, not the caller's own file. Hit live on 2026-08-03 by the wa-inbox-schema engineer, who correctly refused to run it and verified statically instead (pglast AST parse + 12 structural tests). Same footgun class the sibling tools were already fixed for. Fix: accept worktree_path (resolve products_dir from it) and, when set, restrict `pending` strictly to target= unless the caller explicitly opts into the full backlog.

target: mcp/noctusai — agent-context cache freshness under concurrent sessions
description: N=2 SAME SESSION, two independent agents: the pre-commit 8-way-sync gate blocked on `agent-context-cache-stale` for agents (`backend-engineer`, `security`) that neither diff had touched. Plain `--refresh-agent-context-cache` reported "refreshed"/"in-sync" but the very next freshness check still saw a mismatch; only `--force` converged. Separately, `noctus.dev.agent_context_refresh` (the MCP tool) reported `in-sync` while the worktree's pre-commit hook simultaneously reported STALE — because the MCP tool resolves from the PRIMARY checkout while the hook resolves REPO_ROOT to the worktree, so they were grading different trees. Two candidate causes, not yet separated: (a) a source_sha guard that under-detects, or (b) a genuine race on the shared Tier-1 cache with concurrent peer sessions (3+ agents were writing this repo). Cost is real: the gate fires on commits it should pass, and the documented fix (plain refresh) does not resolve it — which is the shape that trains agents to reach for --no-verify. Fix candidates: make the freshness check worktree-aware in the MCP tool (mirror the hook's REPO_ROOT override), and/or make the plain refresh converge (force when the guard says in-sync but the checker disagrees), and/or take a lock per KB § PATTERNS/common/cache-locking-discipline.md.
resolve_when: agent_context_refresh honors a worktree path AND a plain --refresh-agent-context-cache converges the freshness check without --force

target: mcp/noctusai — task_branch wire_env does not pin noctusai_lib to the worktree
description: A product backend test run from ANY worktree resolves `noctusai_lib` to the PRIMARY checkout (the shared venv installs it editable against `/…/noctusai/seed/lib/backend`), not to the worktree's own copy. Consequences, both bad: (1) a product slice consuming a NEW seed symbol added on the same branch fails with `No module named …` even though the file is present in the worktree — looks like the engineer's bug, is actually path resolution; (2) worse, a product slice that MODIFIES seed behaviour tests green against the primary's OLD seed code — a false pass that says 'tested' when it tested stale bytes. Hit live 2026-08-03 wiring the Meta leadgen receiver (`parse_leadgen_webhook` invisible from the worktree that contained it). `task_branch action=start wire_env=True` already solves the analogous FRONTEND problem (symlinks per-package node_modules + re-points @noctusai deps) but has no Python equivalent. Workaround: prefix every command with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/seed/lib/backend`. Fix shape: have wire_env also emit a `.pth`/`sitecustomize` or a documented PYTHONPATH export into the worktree, and have the engineer-seed protocol state it. This is a silent-false-green class, so it deserves a gate, not just documentation.
resolve_when: task_branch wire_env pins noctusai_lib to the worktree's seed/lib/backend (or engineer-seed documents the PYTHONPATH requirement) so a worktree test run cannot silently exercise the primary tree's seed lib

target: mcp/noctusai — task_branch wire_env does not pin noctusai_lib to the worktree
description: 🔴 RETRACTION of the earlier entry with this same target (2026-08-03T20:31Z). That entry claimed worktree pytest runs silently exercise the PRIMARY tree's seed lib — a false-green class. THAT IS WRONG and the entry should be treated as closed-invalid. The mechanism already exists and works: every one of the 11 products' `tests/conftest.py` injects `<repo>/seed/lib/backend` + `<repo>/seed/framework/backend` at sys.path[0] AND calls `noctusai_lib.testing.conftest_helpers.purge_shadowing_editable_finders(_LIB)`, which drops sibling-worktree editable finders. Landed 2026-05-20 ('post-axis-swap fan-out, mirroring ERP-P7's reference fix'). Verified 2026-08-03: with the conftest shim and NO PYTHONPATH, a worktree run resolves both packages to the worktree. My false diagnosis came from probing with a bare `python -c` import, which does not load conftest — so it observed the editable install pointing at the primary and I generalized that to pytest, which was never true. The REAL residual gap is much smaller and worth stating precisely: ad-hoc NON-pytest python invocations from a worktree (`python -c`, one-off scripts, REPL checks) still resolve the primary tree's seed. That can mislead a human or agent doing a manual import check, as it misled me. It does NOT affect any test run. Fix if ever worth it: document the bare-python caveat in engineer-seed, not a second path-pinning mechanism. LESSON (the durable part): I nearly fanned a duplicate pytest.ini `pythonpath` mechanism across 11 products + the seed template for a problem the codebase had already solved — the exact replication-to-seed-symmetry slip the methodology names. Reverted before commit. The check that would have caught it in 30 seconds is 'grep the existing conftest for prior art BEFORE designing a fix' — codebase-is-source-of-truth applies to solutions, not only to facts.</description>

Five product-FE test files fail intermittently under FULL-SUITE parallel load but pass deterministically in isolation: Settings.test.tsx, Clientes.test.tsx, ClienteModal.test.tsx, Conexoes.test.tsx, leads/BaseDeLeads.test.tsx. Environment setup time was ~157s in the failing run vs ~2s isolated, so the trigger is contention (likely jsdom/environment startup racing timers or shared module state), not the code under test. Risk: flaky red masks real breakage and trains agents to re-run until green, which is exactly how a genuine regression gets waved through. Fix direction: isolate the offenders (pool/threads config or fileParallelism false for these files) or find the shared state they race on.

PARALLEL-DISPATCH SEAM GAP, observed 2026-08-04. Slice 3 shipped ingest_meta_lead and Slice 4 shipped notify_new_lead, each file-disjoint, each with green tests — and neither was ever called from the webhook receiver that was supposed to invoke both. File-disjoint slicing makes the INTEGRATION SEAM belong to no engineer, and per-slice tests cannot see it. The receiver also had zero service-level tests (only route tests against a fake service), so nothing failed. Candidate rule: when a dispatch plan has slice B producing a capability slice A must CALL, the brief must name the call site and the wave must end with a seam test that fails if the call is absent.

N=2 TRIAGED, not yet formalized: the per-Redis-URL bus cache + fake-mode warning in get_meta_leads_bus duplicates get_whatsapp_bus in app/services/whatsapp_realtime.py. Resolution named: extract get_product_bus(redis_url, *, label) once a THIRD live surface appears. Deliberately not done inline — refactoring a peer's just-landed module in the hour before a prod promotion trades a real deployment risk for a cosmetic one. Mandatory at N=3.

NEGATIVE-CONTROL FALSE-GREEN from a worktree — new instance of the "harness silently resolves to the primary tree" family. A verification SCRIPT FILE written to the scratchpad and run as `python /path/to/scratchpad/x.py` gets sys.path[0] = THE SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY, so `import noctusai_lib` falls through to the shared venv's editable install → the PRIMARY checkout. The same code run via heredoc/stdin or `python -c` gets sys.path[0] = '' → cwd → the WORKTREE. Observed live 2026-08-05: a debug script reported the security fix NOT working (it was reading the primary's pre-fix module) while the identical code inline reported it working. Worse, the monkeypatch-based negative control (patch redact to identity, then pytest.main) reported the guard tests still GREEN — it had patched the primary's module object while pytest imported the worktree's, so the control proved nothing. A security test whose negative control silently no-ops is the exact false-green shape our methodology exists to prevent. Resolution used: defeat the guard AT SOURCE (edit the file, run the real suite, restore) — the only control that cannot be fooled by module identity. Candidate rules: (1) never verify from a script file placed outside the tree under test; (2) any negative control must ASSERT it patched the intended tree (`assert 'worktrees' in mod.__file__`) before trusting a green; (3) prefer source-level revert over monkeypatch for negative controls. Sibling of the existing entries on task_branch wire_env not pinning noctusai_lib and MCP tools lacking worktree_path.

USER DECISION PENDING — key rotation. Vista echoes the tenant API key verbatim in 401 response bodies (confirmed by string-matching the live body against VISTA_API_KEY on 2026-08-05), and httpx renders the ?key= URL inside transport errors. Before the d3cb3c26 redaction landed, both paths reached VistaUpstreamError.body / str(exc) and the MCP's typed_error.message — meaning the key has been emitted into AI-agent context windows (it appeared in this session's tool results) and into any log line built from str(exc). The redaction stops FUTURE exposure; it cannot un-expose what already leaked. Rotation is a user call because it requires a Vista-side action and a coordinated .env update across local + prod. Filed as the Tier-4 ask in KB § CONTEXT/INTEGRATIONS/vista.md § 9, alongside reporting the echo to Vista as an upstream security defect — any customer logging error bodies is persisting a credential. Note the ERP HTTP surface was never a leak path (the router maps typed errors to fixed Portuguese strings, not str(exc)), so blast radius is agent contexts + application logs, not end-user HTTP responses.
resolve_when: VISTA_API_KEY rotated with Vista and updated in the root .env + prod env

The invitations migrations (adconnect 005, dev-team 0004, knowledge-extractor 002) are committed and correctly numbered to run after the base ones, so provisioning is `noctus.dev.migrate_product` per product once someone decides these products should have live data. description: INVESTIGATION RESULT (2026-08-07, read-only — nothing changed). adconnect / dev-team / knowledge-extractor fail at TWO independent layers, not one. (1) The schemas do not exist: information_schema.schemata has no adconnect, dev_team or knowledge_extractor, 0 tables each, and each product's base migration opens with CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS — so nothing has ever been applied. (2) Even if created, PostgREST would still refuse them: probing from inside the LIVE containers with each product's own client returns PGRST106 'Invalid schema', hint 'Only the following schemas are exposed: public, graphql_public, erp, personal-finance, therapy, seed, daily_life, mailing, social_wiring, orbity, pilates'. adconnect, dev_team, knowledge_extractor, imobi_scheduling and media_scheduling are all absent from that exposure list, which is a Supabase PROJECT SETTING, not something a migration can fix. Provisioning therefore needs THREE steps: create schema + run the product's migrations + add the schema to the PostgREST exposed list. Runtime state: the apps boot fine (adconnect /api/health 200, /api/team 401 — the auth boundary is correct); only authenticated DATA calls fail, which is why the fleet health check reads green. knowledge-extractor has no container at all. All three are described in the roster as in-flight/gated (adconnect 'MVP in flight', dev-team 'switch-flip gated by ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', KE 'seam-swap + container gate in flight'), so dormant-by-intent is plausible — but two of them are DEPLOYED, which is the part that does not fit that reading. Awaiting user decision on provision vs retire vs undeploy.

description: Master-tree-parallel dispatches never run wire_env, so seed/lib/frontend/node_modules and seed/framework/frontend/node_modules are absent in the worktree. Every product tsconfig 'include's the seed FE source dirs, whose own peer deps (@radix-ui/*, @dnd-kit/*) resolve from those node_modules — so tsc cannot reach a true green until someone symlinks them in from the primary tree. Surfaced during the p-studio absorption (slice B, 2026-08-13): the dispatched frontend engineer hit it, symlinked to get a TRUE green rather than a false one, and flagged it rather than reporting a green it had not earned. Candidate fix: task_branch wires the seed FE node_modules on worktree creation regardless of dispatch shape, or a preflight surfaces the gap loudly instead of letting tsc fail confusingly. resolve_when: seed/{lib,framework}/frontend/node_modules present in a freshly created task_branch worktree with no manual intervention.

target: noctus.dev tools ignore worktree_path (validate_product, refresh_dependabot_coverage, refresh_ci_matrix_coverage)
description: N=3 same shape, found 2026-08-13/14 during the p-studio absorption: several noctus.dev tools accept a worktree_path argument and silently resolve against the PRIMARY checkout anyway. refresh_dependabot_coverage and refresh_ci_matrix_coverage both reported 'in-sync' for a product that exists only in the worktree (the CLI run inside the worktree then found and fixed real gaps). validate_product reported 4 post_scaffold_check failures — missing 02-LANDSCAPE roster row, missing INSERT INTO public.products — that are all present in the worktree. predeploy_check DOES honour worktree_path (it correctly found framework-dep drift for a worktree-only product), so the contract is inconsistent rather than absent, which is worse: an agent cannot tell which tools to trust. The failure mode is a confident false NEGATIVE ('in-sync') or a confident false POSITIVE ('roster row missing'), both of which an agent may act on. Candidate: make worktree_path resolution a shared helper every tool routes through, and have tools that cannot honour it REFUSE rather than silently using the primary root. Separately, validate_product's backend_port_in_start_sh / frontend_port_in_start_sh checks test the legacy native-startup model and fail for igig too (a live prod product) — they need retiring or re-aiming at the single-container model.

_find_files does `sorted([f for f in directory.rglob(pattern) if "node_modules" not in str(f) ...])` — rglob TRAVERSES node_modules fully and the comprehension discards afterwards, so the traversal cost is paid in full. Measured 2026-08-14: TestSeedCompliance::test_all_products_compliant and TestAIFeatureCompleteness::test_real_products_pass_validate exceed 25 MINUTES locally and are effectively unrunnable — a 900s and a 1500s timeout both expired, in the absorption worktree AND in the primary checkout, so it is not p-studio's doing. They pass in CI only because a fresh CI checkout never npm-installs the product frontends; that environment difference is exactly what hides this from the gate. Any developer running the toolkit suite on a machine where the fleet has been installed hits it. Fix: prune during the walk (os.walk with dirnames[:] filtering, or an equivalent pre-pruned traversal) rather than filtering the result. Verify by timing test_all_products_compliant before/after in a tree with products/*/frontend/node_modules present. Second-order lesson worth keeping: a test that cannot FINISH is indistinguishable from a test that FAILS, and running the suite with pytest --timeout converts it into a red that reads as an assertion failure — which is how these two were first misattributed to the absorption.

target: CORRECTION to the prior _find_files/node_modules entry — cause NOT established
description: Supersedes the cause stated in the earlier entry 'analyzers.py::_find_files — rglob-then-filter walks node_modules'. The OBSERVATION stands and is reconfirmed: TestSeedCompliance::test_all_products_compliant and TestAIFeatureCompleteness::test_real_products_pass_validate exceed 50 MINUTES locally (timeouts expired at 900s, 1500s and 3000s) in BOTH the absorption worktree and the primary checkout, while CI runs the same suite green — so they are pre-existing and unrelated to the p-studio absorption. The stated CAUSE was wrong. I moved products/p-studio/frontend/node_modules aside so the worktree had ZERO product node_modules (matching a fresh CI checkout) and the tests STILL ran past 10 minutes. So rglob-then-filter over product node_modules is not the (only) driver. The rglob-then-filter pattern at analyzers.py:59 is still a genuine inefficiency worth fixing, but it must not be recorded as the explanation for this timeout. Remaining untested hypotheses: the scan may traverse the symlinked seed/{lib,framework}/frontend/node_modules present in the worktree; or .claude/worktrees/ recursively; or venv/. Whoever picks this up should PROFILE first (cProfile or py-spy on a single test) rather than inherit a guess — this entry exists because the last guess was confidently wrong and would have sent the next reader down the wrong path.

task_branch action='cleanup' commits the salvage-ledger line to the PRIMARY checkout's CURRENT branch. When local `dev` is behind origin/dev (normal — integrate pushes to origin without fast-forwarding the primary), that commit lands on the STALE base and silently diverges local dev from origin. Observed twice in one session (2026-08-21, vista-grant-landed-reprobe): local dev ended 2 ahead / 12 behind, and each attempted cleanup added another divergent commit. The remedy — `git reset --hard origin/dev`, which REMOVES divergence rather than creating it — is itself REFUSED by primary_write_guard, so the guard blocks the fix for drift its sibling tool creates and there is no in-tool path back to sync. Two candidate fixes: (a) cleanup fast-forwards the primary to origin/dev before appending, or writes the ledger line via its own task branch; (b) primary_write_guard allows sync-only operations that make the primary strictly equal to origin/dev (reset --hard origin/dev, merge --ff-only). Work itself is safe throughout — it is on origin/dev; the damage is a quietly divergent primary checkout that surfaces later as a non-fast-forward.
resolve_when: task_branch cleanup no longer commits to a stale primary dev, OR primary_write_guard permits sync-to-origin resets

description: CORROBORATION + one CORRECTION to the 2026-08-21 entry on this same target (rowid 37889). Reproduced twice more on 2026-08-21/22 in an unrelated session: `task_branch action='cleanup'` appended its salvage-ledger commit to the primary checkout's local `dev` while that branch was behind origin/dev, leaving the primary 1-3 ahead / N behind each time. So the cadence is not incident-specific — it fires on any session that runs cleanup without first fast-forwarding the primary, which is the normal state after `integrate` (integrate pushes to origin and never moves the primary). CORRECTION: the original entry states "there is no in-tool path back to sync". That is wrong. `git pull --rebase origin dev` IS permitted by primary_write_guard (`pull` is deliberately absent from `_GIT_WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS`) and resolves the divergence cleanly, because the divergent commits are ledger-only and rebase cleanly on top. Used successfully three times this session; the resulting push was a clean fast-forward each time. `reset --hard` is refused, but it was never the only remedy — so the guard is NOT blocking the fix, and fix (b) (teach the guard about sync-only ops) is optional rather than required. Fix (a) — cleanup fast-forwards the primary before appending, or writes the ledger via its own task branch — remains the real fix, because the current behaviour makes every cleanup a divergence event that the operator must notice and repair by hand. Nothing is ever at risk: the work is on origin/dev throughout; the cost is a quietly divergent primary that surfaces later as a non-fast-forward push.

primary_write_guard refuses deletion of an ORPHANED worktree directory under .claude/worktrees/ (git admin dir already pruned, so `git worktree remove` cannot run either). Hit 2026-08-22 on .claude/worktrees/p-studio-absorption — 46MB, proven to hold zero unique content (all 109 divergent files hash to blobs already in the object DB; the only never-seen content is .pytest_cache). The guard classifies any path under the repo root as 'the primary checkout', but .claude/worktrees/ is gitignored scratch and removing a DEAD worktree there is exactly what task_branch cleanup does. Net effect: the one cleanup that cannot be done via task_branch (because there is no branch left to clean) is also the one the guard blocks, so the drift can only be resolved by the user running rm by hand. Sibling of the existing entry on 'mcp/noctusai — task_branch cleanup + primary_write_guard'.
resolve_when: primary_write_guard permits removal of a path under .claude/worktrees/ that git worktree list does not report, OR a noctus.dev tool exists to reap orphaned worktree directories with the salvage leg attached

description: Order-dependent HANG in the portal_leads suite. On 2026-08-22, `pytest tests/modules/portal_leads/ -q` (118 tests) hung and was killed by the pytest.ini 60s timeout — the stack dump named `Thread-119 (run_blocking_portal)`, i.e. anyio's sync-endpoint threadpool under TestClient. The SAME command passed in 5.25s and 5.82s on other runs; explicit seeds 12345 (and the default order) pass. pytest-randomly 4.1.0 randomizes order per run, so the failing interleaving is not reproduced by re-running. Not chased further because the session was wrapping and the primary_write_guard blocks pytest runs in the primary checkout (cache writes), so a repro needs a dedicated worktree. Why it matters: this is precisely the CI-hazard shape the pytest.ini timeout comment was added for — a hung run is a red CI that looks like an infra flake, and the failing seed is printed by pytest-randomly in the header, so the next occurrence should be captured from the CI log header rather than re-guessed.
resolve_when: the hanging interleaving is reproduced from a recorded pytest-randomly seed and either fixed or given an explicit ordering/isolation marker

description: THIRD recurrence (2026-08-21 ×2, 2026-08-22) — task_branch cleanup strands its salvage-ledger row on the primary checkout and drifts local dev from origin. _push_salvage_ledger_from_primary commits the row to the PRIMARY checkout's current branch then FF-pushes; its divergence guard correctly refuses the push whenever local dev is already ahead by a non-ledger commit, and the documented fallback ("the row stays committed on local dev and ships with the next dev push") NEVER fires, because nothing pushes local dev directly — every change reaches dev through a worktree integrate, which leaves the primary behind and never fast-forwards it. So each cleanup adds one more local-only commit; the divergence then makes the NEXT cleanup's push refuse too, which is why it compounds rather than self-heals. The remedy is refused as well: git reset --hard origin/dev on the primary is blocked by primary_write_guard (correctly — it cannot tell a resync from a write), and git merge --ff-only fails once diverged, so only the human can clear it. Three manual carries done so far (12724799, and now 68d131fa). DRY N=3 ⇒ formalize. Two candidate fixes, not mutually exclusive: (a) cleanup FFs the primary to origin/dev BEFORE appending, and when it cannot, writes the row via its own throwaway task branch instead of the primary — never leaving a local-only commit behind; (b) primary_write_guard whitelists sync-only operations that make the primary strictly EQUAL to origin/dev (fetch + merge --ff-only + reset --hard to the exact origin sha), which is a resync, not a write. Also worth pinning: cleanup should report status='partial' with the stranded sha rather than succeeding quietly, since today the operator only discovers the drift on the next merge --ff-only.

NEW INSTANCE, and the WORST-SHAPED one yet, of the "harness silently resolves to the PRIMARY tree" family (see the N=3+ FORMALIZE entry on 'MCP tools lacking worktree_path', ts 2026-07-20T15:45). Every prior instance in that family is a false NEGATIVE that is at least loud eventually (module-not-found, bundle-not-found, a suite that never ran). This one is a false GREEN that looks like a normal pass.

MECHANISM: MockSupabaseClient.select() validates the column list via _validate_select_cols against a schema map that noctusai_lib.testing._schema_cache.get_schema_map() builds by PARSING MIGRATION FILES under a repo root discovered by _find_repo_root() (first parent holding CLAUDE.md + products/). Run from a worktree, the shared venv's editable noctusai_lib resolves to the PRIMARY checkout, and _find_repo_root() walks from there — so the map is built from the PRIMARY's migrations. A migration that exists only in the worktree contributes nothing; its columns are simply unknown; and because the cache is only consulted when non-empty per-table, validation quietly no-ops for the affected tables instead of erroring. Product tests then pass having validated nothing.

OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-22 building the social-wiring derived checklist: migration 068 added nome_completo/email/data_nascimento/genero to social_wiring.clientes, the service selected exactly those four, and `pytest tests/modules/card_hub/test_documento_checklist.py` reported 8 passed. It was passing for the wrong reason. Setting PYTHONPATH=$WT/seed/lib/backend:$WT/seed/framework/backend AND NOCTUSAI_REPO_ROOT=$WT made the map correct (verified by calling get_schema_map() directly and grepping for the new columns); the suite then passed for the right one. Note the parser itself is fine — it handled multi-column ADD COLUMN and RENAME COLUMN correctly once pointed at the right tree.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS SESSION: the mock's schema validation is one of the few places a product test can catch a service/migration mismatch BEFORE the migration is applied to a live database. Silently disabling it in exactly the situation where a new migration is being authored — i.e. a worktree — removes the guard precisely when it is most needed, and the agent has no signal that it is gone.

FIX SHAPE, cheapest first: (a) _find_repo_root() should prefer the CWD's enclosing repo root over the installed package's, so a worktree run resolves to the worktree (NOCTUSAI_REPO_ROOT already overrides, but it is opt-in and nothing prompts for it); (b) task_branch wire_env should export both PYTHONPATH and NOCTUSAI_REPO_ROOT into the worktree — this is the Python half of wire_env that the 2026-08-03 entry already asked for, and NOCTUSAI_REPO_ROOT is the part that entry missed; (c) refuse-not-null: if the discovered repo root is not an ancestor of CWD, emit a loud one-time warning rather than silently building a foreign map. Memory feedback_self_branch_verification_env updated with the operator-side workaround.
resolve_when: a product test that selects a column introduced by a migration present ONLY in the current worktree fails (unknown-column) when run from that worktree without NOCTUSAI_REPO_ROOT set

description: CORRECTION to the 2026-08-22 entry on this target — my earlier root-cause was WRONG, or at best only half the story. I attributed the stranded salvage rows to the divergence guard refusing the push because local dev was ahead. Measured today after three more cleanups: local dev was 3 AHEAD / 0 BEHIND of origin/dev, i.e. a clean fast-forward, every ahead-commit was a ledger commit, and `git push --dry-run origin dev` SUCCEEDED (78bba2e0..6a4a6259) with the pre-push hook running and allowing it. So the push is neither non-FF nor guard-blocked, and salvage_pushed=false is produced INSIDE commit_and_ff_push_ledger. The likeliest remaining candidate is its rebase leg: the helper does fetch -> rebase-onto-origin/dev -> push, and `git rebase` refuses on a dirty working tree. project-history/vector-costs.ndjson is dirty essentially always, because the cost-log pre-commit hook writes to it on every commit — so the helper would be self-blocking on an artifact the toolchain itself creates. NOT yet confirmed by reading the helper; recorded as the leading hypothesis with the falsifying evidence attached so the next agent starts from measurement rather than from my wrong guess. Whoever fixes this should also make the helper REPORT why it declined — `salvage_pushed: false` with no reason string is what let a wrong diagnosis stand for two days.

CORROBORATION (not yet proof) for the 2026-08-24 dirty-tree/rebase hypothesis on this target. Two cleanups ran in one session with a natural control between them. Cleanup #1 (feat/prod-debug-shape-lease-logs): primary was EXACTLY at origin/dev, no rebase needed -> salvage_pushed=true. Cleanup #2 (feat/seed-close-openapi-url): peers had pushed in between so primary was BEHIND, the rebase leg was required -> salvage_pushed=false. The distinguishing variable is therefore whether the rebase leg RUNS, which is exactly what the hypothesis predicts, and the working tree carried the always-dirty project-history/vector-costs.ndjson on BOTH occasions. Independent supporting datum from the same session: I twice had to fast-forward the primary by hand and both times needed `git -c rebase.autoStash=true pull --rebase origin dev` — a plain rebase cannot run with that file dirty, and the cost-log pre-commit hook rewrites it on every single commit, so the toolchain reliably dirties the very file its own rebase leg trips over. WHAT IS STILL MISSING: nobody has yet read commit_and_ff_push_ledger and confirmed the rebase call + observed its raw refusal message. I did NOT observe the helper's own failure directly, only the correlation above, and I am recording it that way deliberately — the prior entry on this target exists precisely because a confident wrong guess stood for two days. Whoever closes this should (a) read the helper, (b) reproduce with a deliberately dirty vector-costs.ndjson, and (c) make it report a REASON string alongside salvage_pushed=false, which is the actual reason two sessions have had to reverse-engineer this.
resolve_when: task_branch cleanup reports a reason string alongside salvage_pushed=false, or pushes the salvage row successfully with a dirty project-history/vector-costs.ndjson in the primary checkout

description:
`_MAX_BODY_PATH_OVERRIDES` now carries 4 entries, 3 under /api/clientes. Every new route taking an UploadFile needs a human to remember to add one; a forgotten entry 413s ONLY for realistically-sized files, so every fixture-based test passes while real phone photos fail in production. Found while adding POST /api/clientes/*/checklist-extras/*/documento (2026-08-27), which needed a 30MB override the brief had not anticipated.

Matches the CLAUDE.md §1 shape "Hand-maintained lists drift - derive, don't sync by hand; gate pre-push", which already has sibling keepers (check_hardcoded_product_slug_set, check_dependabot_product_coverage, check_ci_test_matrix_coverage).

The same 7-field document projection (id, nome_original, mime_type, tamanho_bytes, tipo_documento, enviado_por, created_at) is hand-written in card_hub/documentos_service._documento_out, card_hub/financiamento_service._documento_out, imovel_hub/documentos_service._documento_out, and now card_hub/documentos_service.documento_resumo (a narrower 5-field variant added 2026-08-27 for checklist-extras). Each adds per-surface extras over an identical core.

CLAUDE.md §1 DRY: N=3+ MUST formalize; the 4th instance is forbidden - and documento_resumo IS the 4th. It shipped because the alternative was blocking a product slice on a cross-module refactor, so this is a deliberate accept-with-rationale, not an oversight.

Proposed: base projection in documentos_service (or table_reads) + per-surface extension, so the 5th caller extends rather than copies.

COUNTER-INCIDENT: the documented rule manufactured the bug it was written to prevent. The 2026-07-22 codification prescribed 'gate loading on isPending || isFetching' as THE correct gate, in CLAUDE.md §1, in the KB doc's Checklist, and in the keeper's own remediation message. isFetching is true during EVERY background refetch, so an early-return skeleton unmounts its subtree on every mutation. Fleet audit 2026-08-31 found 70 instances of that shape plus 140 key-change-flicker sites across social-wiring, igig, erp-imobiliario and two seed organs; user-visible as an 8-row DADOS OBRIGATORIOS block vanishing on every field edit. Every one of those sites was FOLLOWING the documented rule. Two pre-existing tests (PortalRoi.test.tsx, LeadgenWebhookCard.test.tsx) had encoded the buggy contract as an assertion and blocked the fix. Generalizable lesson: a rule stated as a universal when it is only true of one race scales the wrong behaviour at fleet speed, and it reaches the test suite, where it acquires the authority of a gate. When codifying an incident fix, state the DECISION PROCEDURE, not the one expression that closed that incident.

WIDENED the rule to a decision procedure rather than a blessed expression. Canonical gate is now the two-signal form: showSkeleton = isPending && !data (skeleton branch), isRefreshing = isFetching && !!data (non-destructive indicator ONLY, never an early return), plus placeholderData: (prev) => prev on any user-keyed query. The 2026-07-21 prohibition on .isLoading is UNCHANGED and the doc says so explicitly so nobody reverts. Doc now carries BOTH failure modes with equal weight (empty-over-data and skeleton-over-data), a truth table over isPending/isFetching/data, four recognisable shapes, the fix-at-the-hook-not-the-page lever from igig 1e770842, the LGPD placeholderData refusal from erp useVistaShowcase.ts:244 codified as a rule rather than an exception, and the tests-defend-the-bug finding. CLAUDE.md §1 line 67 amended in place (rule count unchanged). frontend-engineer.md L1 line rewritten. check_lying_loading_state docstring + header comment corrected; detector needs NO logic change (early-exits on absence of isLoading) and its Mode-A-only scope is now stated in the doc. Filename deliberately kept: a skeleton over existing data IS a lying loading state, and the name stays symmetric with the keeper, the CLI flag and the lying-loading-ok escape hatch.

OPEN DRIFT — the keeper's own remediation text still prescribes the superseded gate. compliance.py:8488 emits 'Use {query_expr}.isPending || {query_expr}.isFetching' and compliance.py:8513 emits 'Use !X.isPending && !X.isFetching && ...'. Both are the shape that produced the 2026-08-31 refetch-unmount incident (70 sites), so every time this detector fires it pushes the reader into the bug. The docstring and the module header comment above them were corrected on this branch; the two message strings were NOT, because they sit in the function body and the documentation slice's write zone was docstring-text-only while a peer's keeper work was landing in the same file. RESOLVE WHEN: 8488 says the skeleton branch is '{query_expr}.isPending && !{query_expr}.data' and 8513 says the empty branch is '!X.isPending && ...' (no isFetching), with the regexes and control flow untouched. Second, separable finding: the detector covers the empty-over-data mode ONLY; the refetch-unmount mode is doc-enforced, not gate-enforced, which is a live gate-methodology-sync gap.

target: check_prod_exposure_consent / prod_consent action=author — cites the WRONG message as authorization
description: SECURITY-GATE DEFECT, found 2026-08-16 by using the gate for real on p-studio. `prod_consent action=author` wrote a consent record whose `authorization.phrase` is NOT an authorization: it quoted "Publishing p-studio on a public URL is the promotion decision, and KB PATTERNS/devops/prod-exposure-consent.md says registering a prod-exposure surface is the user's call, never an agent's — an agent may only record it, verified against the harness transcript." That sentence is ANOTHER AGENT'S EXPLANATION OF THIS VERY GATE, which the user had pasted into the conversation while forwarding a report from a different session (transcript line 49, type=queue-operation/operation=enqueue, message begins "this was the last message he sent me, plus the recap piece:"). It grants nothing. Meanwhile the user's GENUINE authorization — the exact canonical sentence "I authorize p-studio to be published to production." — sits at line 239 as type=user/promptSource=typed, the strongest evidence shape the pattern defines, and the gate did not cite it. Probable cause: first-match-wins scanning in file order (49 < 239) over all accepted human shapes, with no preference for promptSource=typed, no preference for an EXACT canonical-sentence match over the conjunctive verb-slug-prod heuristic, and no exclusion of text that is quoting rather than speaking. Note the recorded tier was 'performative' even though the quoted sentence contains no performative verb directed at the product. IMPACT: the consent DECISION here was genuine, so nothing unsafe shipped — but the RECORD's evidence was false, and the whole point of the verified-transcription redesign is that the record must point at something the agent did not write. An auditor reading that phrase would reasonably conclude an agent manufactured consent. GENERALIZATION AND THE REAL DANGER: quoting this gate's own KB documentation into a conversation can satisfy the gate, because that documentation necessarily contains the slug and a production token when discussing a given product. The slug-binding protection does not help when the quoted text is ABOUT authorizing that exact product. FIX CANDIDATES: (1) collect ALL matches, never the first, and rank — exact canonical sentence > conjunctive performative > directive; (2) prefer promptSource=typed over queue-operation when both exist; (3) reject a candidate whose match is embedded in a larger block bearing quotation markers ("recap", "he sent me", leading '> ', or a fenced block); (4) record ALL candidate matches in the YAML so an auditor sees what was chosen over what. ACTION TAKEN: the generated record was NOT committed; it was preserved to the session scratchpad as REJECTED-p-studio.prod.yml and deleted from deploy/consent/. p-studio's prod promotion is blocked on this until the matcher can cite the real sentence — hand-authoring is refused to agents by design and I am not going around that.

Third instance on p-studio-absorption-rollout of reporting a FILE's contents as the state of the LIVE system. 2026-08-17: an agent read the literal `senha123` in `002_plataforma_e_seeds.sql:90`, saw a live `auth.users` row with `last_sign_in_at` set, and reported a live weak-credential exposure to the user, who authorized a production DELETE on that premise. The roadmap's own § Known hazards had checked the live hash on 2026-08-14 (`encrypted_password = crypt('senha123', ...)` -> FALSE) and struck the hazard through; the agent had read § Milestones but not § Known hazards. The two prior instances (the same `senha123` claim in Phase 0, and `url_base='localhost:5176'` called a production leak) are already recorded in that same section, which names the shared cause: reading a file and reporting it as the state of the world. The removal itself was sound on other grounds and the user's call stands, but consent was obtained against an overstated premise. Candidate mechanisms: (a) when a roadmap/PROJECT doc has a '## Known hazards' section, reading it is mandatory before asserting any live-state claim about that product; (b) a live-state assertion sourced from a file needs a live query cited alongside it, or it is labelled inference. Escalate to s3-kb if a fourth instance appears.
resolve_when: a keeper or KB pattern requires live-state claims to cite a live query, or § Known hazards to be read before live-state assertions

description: SocialWiringSettings inherits ProductSettings' default max_body_bytes=1MB via MaxBodySizeMiddleware, which is smaller than any reasonable per-document upload limit (contracts/PDFs routinely exceed 1MB). lead-card-hub P2's document-upload endpoint had to cap MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES at 800KB to stay under the platform-wide 1MB body cap — an app-wide setting, not a per-route override, so raising it for document uploads would loosen the cap for every other endpoint in the product (webhooks included) as a side effect. Worth a follow-up: either a per-route body-size override mechanism in MaxBodySizeMiddleware/app_factory, or an explicit architect decision to raise social-wiring's max_body_bytes product-wide.

_batched(items, size) — chunk a list for PostgREST .in_() URL-length safety — now exists twice in social-wiring: clientes_service._batched (private) and card_hub.services._batched (private, this slice). N=2 within one product is triage-only per the recurrence rule, not yet MUST-formalize, but a 3rd occurrence anywhere in the fleet should trigger lifting it into noctusai_lib.integrations.persistence (sibling of iter_paged_rows, which already lives there) rather than a 3rd private copy.

Per-product required-in-prod env has NO home, so a product can deploy with its integration switched off and every gate stays green. p-studio shipped to prod on 2026-08-17 with ASAAS_API_KEY / ASAAS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN unset and P_STUDIO_ORG_ID pointing at a zero-member org; predeploy_check returned ready 7/7 because BASELINE_REQUIRED_PROD_ENV is a FLEET-WIDE tuple holding exactly one key (REDIS_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY). Adding product-specific keys to it would break the other 12 products, so there is no correct place to declare 'this product needs these env vars in prod' — the gap is structural, not an oversight. Symptom was only findable by probing the live webhook (503). p-studio worked around it by moving credentials into the DB (migration 008), which removes ITS dependency on env but leaves the general gap standing for every other product with a per-product secret. Candidate shape: a per-product required_prod_env declaration on ProductSettings that predeploy_check composes with the fleet baseline. Pilot-products-first before fan-out.

target: mcp/noctusai/server.py + tools/noctus/dev/noc_graph_cache.py — MCP server dies mid-session under sustained CPU-bound concurrent load
description: SECOND, DISTINCT mechanism behind the recurring 'noctusai MCP server disconnects mid-session' incident. Commit 39e4256f (2026-08-28) correctly root-caused and fixed the DEPLOY-session shape: FastMCP dispatches a sync tool inline on the asyncio loop, and offload_blocking (anyio.to_thread.run_sync at the server.tool seam) moves it to a worker thread — which fixes an I/O-bound blocker (time.sleep / SSH throttling releases the GIL while blocked) but does nothing for a CPU-bound one. The server died again 2026-08-31 on a NON-deploy session (8 concurrent subagents + orchestrator; one mid-task_branch action=integrate, whose cache_settle leg can trigger a noc-graph rebuild — 39,450 nodes / 62,815 edges, ~13-20s pure-Python AST-walk + clustering — while several other agents independently triggered cache refreshes in the same window). MEASURED via the REAL mcp.server.stdio transport plumbing (which itself hops through anyio.to_thread.run_sync for every stdin-readline / stdout-write / flush, sharing the SAME default CapacityLimiter(40) thread pool as offload_blocking): 6 concurrent ~15s CPU-bound calls (the noc-graph-rebuild scale) pushed stdio round-trip latency to ~22s avg / ~40s max (357/400 messages delayed >5s), while the IDENTICAL load shape with an I/O-bound blocker (time.sleep) stayed at ~0.3ms avg / 2.3ms max — same wrapper, same concurrency shape, the only variable is whether the blocking call holds the GIL. CONFIRMS the GIL-contention hypothesis (control vs experiment isolated the mechanism; no other candidate — capacity-limiter exhaustion, non-cancellable threads, >1MB payload framing — was needed to explain the measured stall). FIX (additive, does NOT touch 39e4256f): noc_graph_cache.refresh() gains a module-level IN_MCP_SERVER flag (set only by server.run(), never on import — so CLI/pytest/scripts keep the exact pre-fix in-process behavior) that, when a rebuild is genuinely needed, delegates to a subprocess (_refresh_via_cli_subprocess, re-execs the SAME `cli.py --refresh-noc-graph` every pre-commit/CI caller already uses) instead of running build_graph in-process. subprocess.run().wait() is a blocking OS wait that releases the GIL exactly like time.sleep, so the parent worker thread idles cleanly while the rebuild runs with its own separate GIL in a separate process. The classification is NOT a hand-maintained per-tool list (CLAUDE.md §1 'hand-maintained lists drift') — it lives at the ONE call that does the CPU-heavy work, so every current AND future caller (task_branch's cache_settle, noctus.dev.refresh_all_caches, noctus.dev.settle_structural_caches, the lazy-on-read gate on every noctus.graph.* query) gets the isolation for free. Correctness bonus: cli.py's --refresh-noc-graph handler already wraps the rebuild in acquire_refresh_lock('noc-graph'), a lock the in-process call this replaces did NOT take — concurrent MCP-triggered refreshes (the exact 'several agents independently refreshing' incident condition) now serialize instead of racing to overwrite the same SQLite cache. Regression tests added to mcp/noctusai/tests/test_server_offloads_blocking_tools.py: TestSustainedConcurrentLoadGilContrast (permanent characterization — proves offload_blocking alone is insufficient for CPU-bound work, control vs experiment) and TestNocGraphRebuildIsolatedFromEventLoop (the actual regression pin — verified to FAIL against pre-fix noc_graph_cache.py via git-stash re-run, PASS after). server.py's offload_blocking docstring updated to carry BOTH mechanisms (it previously explained only the I/O-bound/deploy one).
