description: The dispatching brief for feat/mcp-loop-starvation flagged a known trap found the same day: 'mcp/noctusai/cli.py can return rc=0 on a CRASHED dispatch (a ModuleNotFoundError printed a traceback and still exited 0)'. This matters here because the noc-graph GIL-starvation fix (see the paired entry) now depends on cli.py's exit code for correctness (_refresh_via_cli_subprocess raises on proc.returncode != 0). Investigated but could NOT reproduce within the time-box: (1) a static AST sweep of every `except` handler inside main() found only 2 handlers without a subsequent sys.exit/raise, both catching sqlite3.Error, neither related to ModuleNotFoundError; (2) an empirical repro — shadowing noctusai_lib.graph with a module that raises ModuleNotFoundError, then running `python cli.py --refresh-noc-graph` — correctly exited 1 with the traceback on stderr, confirming the specific call this fix depends on is safe. The originally-observed rc=0-on-crash scenario was not isolated to a specific flag/invocation shape within scope. Surfacing rather than guessing at a fix for an unverified problem (measure-first).
resolve_when: the exact crashing invocation shape is identified (e.g. via a deliberately-broken import under the flag actually used at the time) AND cli.py demonstrably exits nonzero on it, OR a global top-level try/except is found and fixed to always sys.exit(1) on an uncaught exception in main()

description: ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED for the recurring primary/origin divergence loop (6th encounter; 5 prior ledger entries all marked closed while the actual cause survived). `_ledger_push.commit_and_ff_push_ledger`'s push leg rebases onto origin/dev before FF-pushing. `git rebase` refuses on ANY dirty file, and the cost-log pre-commit hook dirties project-history/vector-costs.ndjson on essentially every commit — including the ledger commit made one line earlier. So the rebase was refused ("cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes"), the helper returned committed_locally=True/pushed=False, and the PRIMARY checkout was left diverged from origin/dev, hand-cleared once per session with `git -c rebase.autoStash=true rebase origin/dev`. THE FIX ALREADY EXISTED ONE LEVEL UP: task_branch.integrate solved the identical wall on 2026-05-28 (logged N=5+, "Bug C") by classifying dirty files benign-vs-real and auto-stashing the benign ones around the rebase. The 2026-06-30 DRY lift moved the IDIOM into _ledger_push but left the HARDENING behind in task_branch, silently un-fixing the copy. Both now share tools/noctus/dev/_benign_stash.py. Real work still blocks, but as an explicit status='dirty_blocked' naming the files rather than a mystery divergence. SECOND LESSON: no fake-based test could ever have caught this — every _ledger_push test used a runner whose `rebase` returned a scripted rc regardless of tree state. Pinned in test_ledger_push_realgit.py against REAL git, with a control run proving the old code fails the same scenario (1/1 divergence, row never lands). Also hardened the porcelain parser: the old fixed 3-char offset silently TRUNCATED any non-canonical status line into a different path, which then misclassified as real work. NOT the same as the 2026-06-30 post-checkout 'cost-log churn vs rebase' entry — that guards churn DURING a rebase's checkout step; this is dirt BEFORE the rebase starts, which is part of why this read as already-solved for two months.

target: public migration ledger vs applied schema state
description: Supabase's migration history is NOT a reliable record of what has been applied. Verified 2026-08-31 while applying p_studio 009: `supabase_migration_list` contains p_studio 001-006 and (now) 009, but NOT 007 or 008 — yet both are demonstrably applied (007 removed the dev admin: the `p-studio` org has 0 members; 008 created `p_studio.provedor_credenciais` + `integracao_config`, both of which exist). Same shape for social-wiring: migration 060 (negociacoes_venda -> atendimentos) is absent from the ledger, but `social_wiring.atendimentos` exists and `negociacoes_venda` is gone. So some migrations are applied out-of-band (psql / direct SQL) without being recorded, which means the ledger cannot answer "is migration N applied?" and a replay from migrations alone would not reproduce prod. Candidate resolutions: (a) route every product migration through `noctus.dev.migrate_product` so the per-schema `schema_migrations` table is stamped (p_studio has no such table at all today), or (b) a keeper that diffs declared migration files against a recorded-applied set per product and reports the unrecorded ones. Do NOT auto-apply anything to close the gap — the risk is a double-apply on a non-idempotent migration.
resolve_when: a per-product applied-migration record exists and a gate compares it against products/*/backend/migrations/*.sql

description: THIRD mode of the lying-loading class, found during the Cat-C erp sweep: zero-over-data. `pages/Impostos.tsx`, `pages/Manutencao.tsx`, `pages/Comissoes.tsx` render summary cards as `resumo?.field || 0` with NO loading gate at all, so an unresolved query displays "R$ 0,00". This is worse than Mode A (empty state) or Mode B (skeleton-over-data): a zero does not look like a state, it looks like a legitimate answer, so the reader has no cue that the number simply has not arrived. The doc currently frames the class as two complementary modes; it is three. The distinguishing test is `data === undefined` (not arrived) vs `data.field === 0` (really zero) — a fix that skeletons a genuine zero has replaced one lie with another. Note the shape contains no `isLoading` and no `isFetching`, so NEITHER the existing Mode-A detector nor the Mode-B detector being built this session would catch it; it needs its own predicate (optional-chain or nullish/or-default feeding a numeric display, with no query-state gate in the subtree).
resolve_when: lying-loading-state.md documents zero-over-data as Mode C and a detector or explicit non-detection rationale exists

description: THE DIVERGENCE LOOP IS NOT DISCHARGED. `d0170d92` fixed a real cause but the symptom recurs, so do NOT treat the cause as known — `projects/prod-fleet-swap-handoff/PROJECT.md` §7 and HANDOFF-NEXT-SESSION.md §5 both currently imply it is closed; both are wrong. Reproduced 2026-08-31 AFTER the fix: `task_branch action=cleanup slug=mcp-server-env-dotenv` returned `salvage_pushed: false` and left the primary checkout diverged 8-behind/1-ahead of origin/dev. EVIDENCE: (1) at that moment the primary had exactly ONE dirty file, `project-history/auto-improvement.ndjson`, which IS listed in `_benign_stash.BENIGN_REFRESH_PATTERNS`, so it should have been stashed; (2) a manual `git rebase origin/dev` with that file dirty reproduces `error: cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes`; (3) the same rebase with a clean tree, or with `-c rebase.autoStash=true`, succeeds — so the rebase leg itself is fine and the STASH is what did not happen; (4) `commit_and_ff_push_ledger`'s ordering reads correctly in source (commit -> classify_dirty -> stash_benign -> rebase -> pop in finally), and the salvage path does route through it via `task_branch._push_salvage_ledger_from_primary`, so the defect is NOT the documented ordering. Unverified hypotheses, none confirmed: `classify_dirty`'s `git status` invocation not seeing the file from the primary-side runner; `stash_benign` returning falsy and being silently skipped; the cache-settle leg (which reported `auto_improvement: rebuilt`) re-dirtying the tree between the stash and the rebase. NOTE the tests at `mcp/noctusai/tests/test_task_branch.py:387/424/459/535` assert both True and False outcomes for `salvage_pushed` against a scripted runner — the same fake-cannot-express-the-failure shape that let the original bug live, so a fake-based test cannot close this; it needs a REAL-git test like `test_ledger_push_realgit.py`. Also note `auto_improvement_log` appends to the working tree WITHOUT committing, so simply calling that tool leaves the primary dirty and is enough to trigger this.
resolve_when: a real-git test reproduces salvage_pushed=false with a benign-dirty tree and passes after the fix, and a cleanup on a behind-primary returns salvage_pushed=true

description: Broader manual AST sweep (beyond the calibrated check_test_status_assertion detector's conservative scope) found ~49 test methods across 7 igig router test files (test_cliente_router, test_comercial_router, test_distribuicao_router, test_esteira_router, test_financeiro_router, test_integracoes_router, test_marca_router, test_pauta_router) that assert on response body via a variable first unwrapped with `.json()`/`.text` (e.g. `body = api.get(...).json()`; later `assert body["x"] == ...`) with no status_code pin anywhere in the method. The production detector deliberately does not flag these (conservative gating: only names assigned directly from `client.<verb>(...)`, not post-`.json()`-unwrapped vars, are tracked as response vars — documented intentional miss in KB § PATTERNS/compliance/testing.md). This is the established authoring convention throughout igig's test suite (extract body once, assert per-field), not a newly-introduced defect. Fixed only the 3 true siblings directly adjacent to the flagged line (test_pauta_router.py TestContadorDeCaracteres — same class, same feature, same shape) per the scoped follow-up brief; NOT mass-rewriting all 49 sites in this dispatch — that is a separate, larger cross-file effort (possibly warranting a detector-scope widening decision first, since widening the detector to catch unwrapped-var patterns would also flag this same shape fleet-wide, not just in igig).

task_branch action=start wire_env=True symlinks node_modules + @noctusai/{lib,seed} but NOT the repo-root .env, which is gitignored and therefore absent from every fresh worktree. createViteConfig sets envDir to the tree root, so a product frontend started from a worktree renders a BLANK PAGE WITH NO CONSOLE ERROR: createProductSupabase throws inside a module before React mounts. Cost ~15min to diagnose during the igig e2e sweep (2026-09-01); the silent failure mode is the expensive part, not the missing link. Fix: wire_env should symlink the root .env alongside node_modules (gitignored ⇒ never staged, same contract as the existing links).

derive_cors_origins(include_all_frontends=True) emits only BACKEND ports (8000-8014) plus 3000/5173 — it never emits the per-product VITE frontend ports (8080/8090/8170/8180/...) that start.sh registers. Correct for the single-container shape (SPA served from the backend port ⇒ same origin, no preflight) and prod is verified fine (core preflight from https://igig.noctusai.com returns 200). But it makes the LEGACY NATIVE path (./start.sh native, uvicorn+vite) broken fleet-wide: every product's vite origin is refused by both core AND its own backend with 'Disallowed CORS origin' on the OPTIONS preflight, so every authed page fails to load. Surfaced during the igig e2e sweep 2026-09-01; worked around locally with an explicit CORS_ORIGINS env. Decide: either fix the derivation to include frontend ports, or retire the native path so it stops presenting as supported.

A hand-rolled test double that is LOOSER than the client it stands in for makes the suite green on a contract that only exists in the suite. social-wiring's ContractFakeMailchimpClient accepted `type=`, `tags=`, `emails=`, `audience_id=` and a pre-hashed `subscriber_hash` that MailchimpClient/HttpxMailchimpClient never declared. The routers were written against the double, 174 tests passed, and SIX endpoints were broken in production (GET /api/mailchimp/templates 500; every member route double-hashed the email and 404'd — verified live 2026-09-01 against https://social.noctusai.com; send_test/set_member_tags/upsert_member/update_campaign TypeError). Only ONE of the six was visible as a 500 in the logs; the rest returned a plausible 404. The generalizable gate is a per-Protocol-method signature-parity test asserting the double accepts no argument the real client rejects — shipped as products/social-wiring/backend/tests/modules/mailchimp/test_double_matches_protocol.py, which found all six from the one reported symptom. Candidate for a keeper (`check_test_double_signature_parity`) so every product's doubles are covered, not just this one.
resolve_when: a keeper or shared test asserts double-vs-real signature parity for integration test doubles beyond social-wiring/mailchimp

description: Third lying-loading-state mode, not covered by the keeper: a query that is SETTLED with no data (isPending=false, isFetching=false, isError=false, data=undefined) renders NOTHING when the page's branches are `{isLoading && ...}` / `{!isLoading && !isError && data?.items.length === 0}` / `{... > 0}`. `undefined === 0` and `undefined > 0` are both false, so all four branches are off and the user sees a blank page with no signal. Observed live on https://social.noctusai.com/email-marketing/templates behind a mailchimp 500 (2026-09-01) and present on 4 social-wiring pages. The keeper covers the isLoading-vs-isPending mode but not the undefined-length hole. Fix adopted: the seed idiom `isPending || (isFetching && empty)` plus an empty branch that treats no-data as empty.
resolve_when: check_lying_loading_state flags a length-comparison branch whose operand can be undefined

description: Endpoint-to-UI parity, measured 2026-09-01 by enumerating the live route table (466 routes) against every /api literal + resolved api.* call in the frontend: ~93% of routes are reachable from the UI. The unsurfaced remainder is dominated by TWO whole modules with zero frontend: (1) app/modules/email_marketing/* (~62 routes: campaigns, contacts, lists, templates, automations+steps, analytics, AI subjects/debrief/deliverability, settings/domains) — the five Email Marketing PAGES consume /api/mailchimp/* instead, so the product ships two email backends and wires only one; (2) app/modules/scheduling/* (15 routes: condominiums, properties, services, users, appointments, appointment-requests, pending-chat-identities, propose). Smaller gaps: media-creation/branding/* (3), youtube/snapshot/run, calendar/oauth+status, card-hub roteiro visitas POST/DELETE (PATCH is wired), documento extracao confirmar/descartar. Decide per module: build the UI, or retire the routes. Neither is a bug today, but both are surface that cannot be exercised.

adconnect's tests/realdb/ self-SKIP cleanly when run alone (18 skipped, no DSN) but ERROR at fixture setup (15 errors) under the FULL suite with pytest-randomly's default ordering; `-p no:randomly` passes clean. So `predeploy_check adconnect` reports status='blocked' on a seed-order lottery rather than on anything real, which trains people to wave the gate through. Surfaced 2026-09-01 during the igig e2e sweep (adconnect is ativo=false / not in build-scope, so it blocked nothing shipped). Fix direction: make the realdb fixtures skip deterministically regardless of ordering, rather than depending on which earlier test last touched the shared app/state.

FALSE-GREEN BY CWD DRIFT — a verification failure mode with the same shape as the piped-tail exit-code footgun already in §1, and worth the same one-line rule. On 2026-09-01 an agent editing a file inside a WORKTREE ran `pytest <relative/path>` four times (ordered + randomized) and reported 'stable, 77 passed'. The shell cwd had silently drifted to the PRIMARY checkout, so pytest loaded the primary's copy of that file — which never had the edits. Real failures had been observed once, then 'disappeared' on re-run and were rationalized as stale bytecode. CI caught the bug twice. Two mechanical defences, both cheap: (1) run verification against ABSOLUTE paths so cwd cannot retarget the check; (2) assert the anchor matched on every scripted string-replacement edit — a no-op `str.replace` returns the original silently, which is how the signature/body mismatch was introduced in the first place. Candidate §1 line alongside 'Verify PASS/FAIL by exit code, never a piped tail'.

CLOSES the 2026-09-01T17:11:05 wire_env/.env entry and the 2026-09-01T17:11:15 cors_registry entry — both FIXED and shipped to prod in 87c6a00e. wire_env now symlinks the repo-root .env AND mcp/noctusai/node/node_modules into a fresh worktree (blank-page-no-console-error, and the ts-morph Mode-B scan degrading to a warning that reads like a detector regression). Native-mode CORS is fixed via an explicit NOCTUS_NATIVE_DEV=1 opt-in set only by `start.sh native`, leaving the single-container house shape byte-identical (verified: 15 origins, zero vite ports, with the opt-in unset). Re-filed because the ORIGINAL two entries carried resolve_when written in SHELL syntax (`grep -q ... path`) rather than the ledger's predicate grammar (`grep_present:<term>@<path>`), so reconcile reported them as 'unknown predicate grammar' and they could never self-close — an open entry that is actually done is exactly the false hot-drift signal the ledger exists to avoid. Note for future filers: the grammar is keeper:/path_exists:/grep_present:/grep_max:/superseded_by: only.

The outline-corpus baseline fires on legitimate feature growth and has no sanctioned re-ratification path — the only documented way to refresh it is to DELETE the whole fixture and let the test regenerate it, which silently absorbs every unrelated regression present at that moment (exactly the corpus-wide regex drift the fixture exists to catch). Hit 2026-09-01: adding 7 lazy routes to social-wiring's App.tsx moved it 36→44 symbols (22.2%), past the ±5%/±1 tolerance, and CI went red on a change with nothing wrong in it. Had to hand-edit the three drifted entries. Compare `noctus.dev.code_ratify` / `kb_ratify`, which exist precisely so a baseline can be advanced deliberately and per-entry. Fix: a `--ratify-outline-baseline [--paths ...]` leg (or fold into code_ratify) that updates only named entries and records who/why, so the refresh is auditable and cannot become a blanket reset.
resolve_when: a per-entry ratification path exists for outline_corpus_baseline.json (not delete-and-regenerate)

description: A local `vite build` without VITE_SAME_ORIGIN=1 bakes `http://localhost:<backend_port>` as the API base, so a locally-served SPA calls a port nothing is listening on and every page shows "Servidor indisponível (…). Verifique se o backend esta rodando." — which reads as a dead backend when the backend is fine. Only the product Dockerfiles set that env; there is no documented host-side recipe for reproducing the single-container shape locally, and nothing in the build output says which base got baked. Cost a full false-alarm debugging round on 2026-09-01 during the social-wiring e2e (the same class as the already-logged worktree `.env` blank-page finding: a build-time env gap presenting as a runtime fault). Fix candidates: have the factory print the resolved API base at build time (one line, makes the wrong build self-evident), and/or document the `SERVE_SPA_DIR=<dist> VITE_SAME_ORIGIN=1` host recipe in the production-deploy guide as the sanctioned way to run the prod shape without Docker.
resolve_when: the vite factory logs the resolved API base at build time, or the single-container host recipe is documented

description: PreToolUse `test_seam_guard` denies a test-file write that patches our own code, making the long-standing `check_no_self_monkeypatch` keeper a backstop rather than the only gate. Predicate extracted to stdlib-only `self_patch_predicate.py` so both ends share ONE definition and the hook can import it under the system interpreter. Adds the ~4s `--check-no-self-monkeypatch` CLI flag with CI-identical regression semantics (the only prior way to run it was the ~15min compliance suite). description: primary_write_guard treats BOTH arguments of `ln -s SOURCE LINK` as write targets, but only LINK is written — SOURCE is a string recorded in the symlink and need not even exist. Consequence observed 2026-09-04: repairing the gitignored symlinks products/social-wiring/frontend/node_modules/@noctusai/{lib,seed} was REFUSED, because the source arg `../../../../../seed/lib/frontend` resolves onto tracked source. The guard's gitignore exemption (_git_ignores, which names node_modules/ as its own example) never got a chance to apply to the real target. Cost: a full agent session declined the repair and handed it back to the user as a manual keystroke, and the user had already said repeatedly they do not want to run commands. Fix: for `ln`, treat only the FINAL positional argument as the write target (and for `ln -t DIR`, the -t argument); the same last-arg-only rule is arguably right for cp/mv/install/rsync, but ln is the one where the source may legitimately be unresolvable. Add a regression test alongside mcp/noctusai/tests/test_primary_write_guard.py asserting `ln -sfn <tracked-relative-source> <gitignored-link>` is ALLOWED.

CI on origin/dev 4eff482b is RED and BLESS IS BLOCKED, entirely from the permutas absorption (05ce788e). Three failing jobs, one root cause each traceable to permutas: (1) `check_framework_deps` reports 12 missing framework peer deps for permutas — and because that check runs inside EVERY product job, it also reds `Product Backend Tests (pytest) (core)` whose own pytest passed 619/9skip; (2) the same check reds the permutas job; (3) `Trivy filesystem scan (deps)` exits 1 on HIGH/CRITICAL, and Dependabot is concurrently filing PRs against products/permutas/frontend (fast-uri, nanoid, browserslist, multi), which strongly implicates the newly-added permutas lockfile. 🔴 DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY ADDING THE 12 DEPS. permutas/frontend is a create-react-app + Redux + styled-components legacy app that imports NEITHER @noctusai/seed NOR @noctusai/lib (verified: zero @noctusai imports in src, zero @noctusai entries in dependencies). check_framework_deps assumes every product frontend consumes the seed framework; permutas does not. Adding the deps would bloat a CRA bundle with libraries it never imports and make the gate assert something false — the work-around-the-gate anti-pattern. The real resolutions are architectural and belong to the permutas owner + architect: (a) scope permutas OUT of check_framework_deps as a divergent-architecture absorption until its frontend is migrated onto the seed framework (a gate change, so it ships with its compliance mechanism per gate-methodology-sync), or (b) treat the absorption as incomplete and port permutas' frontend onto the seed framework as its own project. Separately the Trivy CVEs need the Dependabot permutas PRs merged. Until one of these lands, `release stage='bless'` refuses and nothing on dev — including four unrelated, fully-green feature slices — can reach main or prod.

test_seam_guard is TOOL-scoped, so a test file authored via a Bash heredoc bypasses it entirely. On 2026-09-07 three self-monkeypatch violations (monkeypatch.setattr on our own app.modules.permutas.embeddings attributes) were written that way, passed the local pre-commit, and were only caught by CI's compliance baseline — the exact 'gated at BOTH ends' claim CLAUDE.md §1 makes for this rule. The WRITE end has a hole whenever a file is produced by a shell redirect/heredoc rather than the Write tool. Candidate fixes: extend the guard to Bash commands whose target path matches a test glob, or lift the check into the pre-commit hook so the second end is genuinely independent of which tool wrote the file.
resolve_when: test_seam_guard covers heredoc/shell-authored test files, or pre-commit runs check_no_self_monkeypatch on staged test files

description: MIGRATION LEDGER DRIFT — fleet-wide, and it caused a live prod break. Two apply paths exist and only one records: (A) noctus.dev.migrate_product applies + INSERTs into <schema>.schema_migrations inseparably; (B) the Supabase MCP takes a pasted body, records into supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, and writes NOTHING to the product ledger. No migration file self-records (0 files contain a schema_migrations tail — by design), so recording is coupled to the TOOL, not the act. social_wiring stopped at 093 (2026-09-04 17:50, last Path-A run) while 097-101 went in via Path B 63 min later. CONSEQUENCE: 101 read as unapplied to every check that trusted the ledger, so commit 7f21a0b4 added two columns by EDITING an applied migration — a no-op against the live DB — and shipped code selecting columns that did not exist. Repaired by 102 + restoring 101; re-applying 097-101 through Path A also brought the social_wiring ledger current (93 -> 100 rows, through 103). STILL OPEN, two parts. (1) No gate: check_migration_number_collision is the ONLY migration keeper and both its legs are about the numeric prefix — it never opens a file, reads APPLIED.md, or touches a DB. A backstop keeper (check_migration_applied_ledger_drift, pre-push, needs a DB round-trip) would diff files-on-disk minus <schema>.schema_migrations and cross-check names present in supabase_migrations — a machine-derivable set, no heuristics. But per gate<->methodology sync the real fix is compliance-by-construction: make Path B record, or make Path A able to chunk so Path B is never needed (101 was split into 2 statements for Path B precisely because the operator believed Path A could not — it applied it whole today, so that belief may itself be stale). (2) A SECOND defect: migrate_product derives schema as slug.replace('-','_'), which is WRONG for three products — erp-imobiliario (real schema 'erp'), personal-finance (real schema 'personal-finance', hyphenated), therapy-platform (real schema 'therapy'). Their ledger rows went into empty phantom schemas: erp_imobiliario.schema_migrations claims 043_api_tokens.sql applied while to_regclass('erp_imobiliario.api_tokens') is NULL (the table is at erp.api_tokens, put there by the file's own SET search_path). Those three ledgers actively LIE about what ran. Blast radius: social-wiring was the best-tracked product at 93/100 rows; erp 1/48, orbity 1/15, therapy 1/15, personal-finance 1/12, daily-life 1/8, seed 1/5; core/adconnect/igig/p-studio/dev-team/knowledge-extractor have no schema_migrations table at all. APPLIED.md exists for social-wiring only, is hand-written prose, stops at ~082, and its own header calls itself 'a convenience record, not an authority' — a third source of truth for facts the DB already holds. User decision 2026-09-07: report now, fix in its own slice.
resolve_when: A check_migration_applied_ledger_drift keeper exists AND migrate_product's schema derivation is corrected for erp-imobiliario / personal-finance / therapy-platform

description: TWO ORCHESTRATORS CAN BLESS+PROMOTE CONCURRENTLY — the release chain has no coordination read. On 2026-09-07 a second tech-lead session (b2613b32) blessed at 11:37:10 and promoted at 11:40:38; this session's own bless landed in the 43s window between that promote's prod-backup snapshot (11:37:53) and its prod FF, so it saw main already advanced and prod not yet, and returned the dev==main early exit having done nothing. NO GATE FAILED: CI on 4c35138e went green at 11:32:39, five minutes BEFORE the bless, so the CI-green precondition held; FF-only held; the prod-backup snapshot was taken correctly. What is missing is coordination. noctus.dev.release — the ONLY tool that writes main and prod — contains ZERO references to the branch-tree ledger (grep count 0), so it cannot see that another orchestrator declared itself on_going. Because bless/promote are whole-repo-state operations by design, whoever moves first sweeps the other's in-flight work into production: this session's card-UI commit reached prod in a promote nobody ran for it, and the other session's Gemini slice reached prod un-reviewed — the slice that then needed three blocking fixes (cross-provider vector-space mixing, Gemini spend billed at zero, a self-monkeypatch masking the second). That is the same shape release.py's own comment names for the CI hole it closed in 2026-08-22: 'A doctrine-only gate is not a gate.' THE BLINDNESS IS SYMMETRIC AND PARTLY MINE: the other session DID declare a pointer (feat/gemini-embeddings-provider, role=orchestrator, with permutas/embeddings.py in its paths — a paths_overlap query would have flagged the exact file I later edited). I never read the live map before starting, which branching §4.5 requires status-first, and I never declared my own — task_branch action=start does NOT write a pointer; that is a separate manual noctus.dev.branch_pointer call. Two candidate fixes: (a) release.py consults branch_pointer before bless/promote and BLOCKS (or loudly warns) when another session holds a non-terminal orchestrator pointer whose paths intersect the promote range; (b) task_branch action=start auto-appends the pointer so declaring is compliance-by-construction rather than discipline. Also observed: two stale on_going pointers are polluting the map — feat/gemini-embeddings-provider (merged and in prod, never closed) and feat/igig-foundation (2026-08-09); a map nobody closes becomes a map nobody reads.
resolve_when: noctus.dev.release consults the branch-tree before bless/promote OR task_branch action=start auto-appends a branch pointer

description:
NO CI JOB RUNS `seed/lib/backend/tests/` — 165 test files (~3637 tests) that gate the SHARED library every product imports. `.github/workflows/test.yml` contains exactly two pytest invocations: line 118 `pytest --tb=short -q` per PRODUCT (working-directory `products/<slug>/backend`) and line 676 `pytest mcp/noctusai/tests/`. The seed lib appears in CI only as an editable dep of the toolkit (line 625) and as a bandit scan target (lines 492/516). Note `seed` IS in the product matrix, but that job's working-directory is `products/seed/backend` — a different tree entirely.

FOUND BY CONSEQUENCE, not by audit: on 2026-09-09 a guard was written at `seed/lib/backend/tests/integrations/llm/test_model_catalog_pricing.py` to stop unregistered models costing $0 silently (`estimate_cost_usd` returns 0.0 on a catalog miss, `compute_spend_usd` sums exactly that column, so the org budget guardrail reads zero forever while looking armed). The guard would itself never have run — reproducing its own failure mode one level up. It caught TWO live cases when finally executed by hand: `claude-opus-5` (newly pinned) and `gpt-4.1-mini` (the OCR pin already in production, unpriced since it shipped).

PARTIAL FIX LANDED (060fecf4): that one file moved to `mcp/noctusai/tests/test_model_catalog_pricing.py`, which CI does run, with a header stating why and asking not to move it back. The SYSTEMIC gap is untouched — the other 164 files still never run, and any new seed-lib test written in the obvious place is dead on arrival.

RESOLUTION IS A DECISION, NOT A PATCH. Adding a `seed-lib` matrix entry is ~5 lines, but nobody knows what a first CI run over 3637 never-gated tests surfaces, and the same first-run-sweep triage that governs a new keeper applies (formalize / accept-with-rationale / defer). Cheapest honest sequence: run the suite in CI once as `continue-on-error: true` to size the surface, triage, then make it blocking. Owner's call — flagged, not started.
resolve_when: .github/workflows/test.yml contains a job whose working-directory or pytest target covers seed/lib/backend/tests

description:
NEW VARIANT of the append-only-ledger drift family (see the open entries on task_branch.py from 2026-08-22 / 08-24 / 08-31): rows written by ONE session landed as uncommitted modifications inside ANOTHER session's worktree, and were on no branch at all.

OBSERVED 2026-09-09: rebasing `feat/model-pricing-test-into-ci` failed with `cannot rebase: Your index contains uncommitted changes`. The three dirty files were `project-history/branch-tree.ndjson`, `branch-tree.mirror.ndjson` and `worktree-salvage.ndjson` — and the added rows were NOT mine. They belonged to session 034951b2 (`feat/papel-da-parte-editavel` marked `shipped`, plus the `session-end-sweep` row, both stamped 22:32:43). Verified absent from origin/dev: `git show origin/dev:<each>` matched 0 of them.

WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN THE LOGGED SIBLINGS: the prior entries are about a row STRANDED on the primary (committed, just unpushed — recoverable by anyone who looks). Here the rows were uncommitted in a THIRD tree that their author neither created nor would revisit, and the natural unblocking move — `git checkout -- project-history/` or a reset to get the rebase going — destroys them with no trace. The rebase failure is the ONLY thing that made them visible; an agent using `rebase.autoStash` or `git stash` would have buried them silently.

RECOVERED THIS SESSION (8ee0cea4): rows extracted before any reset, ledgers restored to origin/dev, rebase, rows re-appended, NDJSON validity re-verified (0 malformed lines, diff exactly +3), committed separately as third-party data recovery.

ROOT CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED — recording the observation, not a guess, per the standing correction on this target (a confident wrong root-cause stood for two days). The open question is why a session_end_sweep appended into a foreign worktree's working tree rather than the primary or its own; REPO_ROOT resolution from a sweep running after its own worktree was removed is the obvious suspect and is UNVERIFIED. Whoever closes this should also consider making the ledger append-and-push atomic (write → commit → push, never leave the file dirty), which would make this class structurally impossible rather than merely detectable.
resolve_when: ledger appends are committed+pushed atomically, or a real-git test covers a cross-worktree append

description:
RESOLVED by jobs `seed-backend-tests` + `seed-frontend-tests` in .github/workflows/test.yml, keeper `check_seed_test_root_ci_coverage`, and KB § PATTERNS/devops/product-lockfile-and-slug-drift.md § Sixth axis.

THE ENTRY'S OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG, and that is the part worth keeping. It said "resolution is a decision, not a patch", resting on "nobody knows what a first CI run over 3637 never-gated tests surfaces", and proposed a continue-on-error sizing run then triage. The sizing was a 12-second question: `env -i PATH=... pytest` (no .env, no SUPABASE_* — the environment CI actually has) gives seed/lib/backend 3637 passed / 1 skipped in 8.2s and seed/framework/backend 203 passed in 3.5s. The one skip is a real conditional (the seed's own build paths), not a missing-dep self-skip. So the jobs landed BLOCKING on day one. GENERAL RULE: before deferring an adoption because the fallout is unknown, check whether the fallout is measurable locally in seconds — "unknown" is a claim needing a measurement, not a default. A continue-on-error job nobody revisits is the same silent debt one layer up.

SCOPE WAS WIDER THAN LOGGED. Auditing for siblings found a THIRD root: seed/lib/frontend has 32 spec files / 375 tests and a `test` script, and no workflow ran it either. It LOOKED covered — seed-typecheck.yml has two steps whose working-directory IS seed/lib/frontend, running `npm run check` (tsc --noEmit only). Total actually ungated: 4215 tests across the three packages every product imports or renders.

ROOT CAUSE — THE KEEPER'S DOMAIN, NOT ITS PREDICATE. check_ci_test_matrix_coverage exists precisely for "a suite silently never runs in CI" and could see none of this: its required set comes from _on_disk_products() (products/*) and seed/lib is not a product; that set is also slug-shaped while these roots are path-shaped. No predicate change inside that keeper's domain could have reached them. A gate whose DOMAIN excludes the gap is worse than no gate, because its green reads as an answer. Generalisation: when a keeper closes a class, interrogate its DOMAIN separately from its PREDICATE — the predicate here was right; the domain was products/* only because that is where the first two instances happened to live.

The new keeper matches on the RUN COMMAND, never on working-directory, pinned by test_a_typecheck_only_step_does_not_count_as_coverage — if that assertion ever passes, the keeper has regressed to the predicate that missed 375 tests. Verified load-bearing: 3 high findings on the pre-fix tree, 0 on the fixed one. seed/framework/frontend is correctly absent (zero specs; `vitest run` hard-fails on "no test files found").

STILL OPEN, NOT THIS SLICE: dev_team/tests (158 files) and the mcp/* vendor connectors (1-6 files each) are also unrun by CI — tooling rather than shipped product code, a genuinely separate decision.

ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED FROM THE CODE (the prior row deliberately recorded no cause, per the standing correction on this target that a confident wrong diagnosis stood for two days). It is not REPO_ROOT resolution, which was the obvious suspect and is wrong.

`.git/refs/stash` is ONE stack for the whole repository — the primary checkout and every worktree share it. `_benign_stash.pop_stash` ran a bare `git stash pop`, i.e. `stash@{0}`, and both callers ran it with their OWN tree as cwd (`task_branch._pop_stash` passes `-C <worktree>`; `_ledger_push` uses the caller's root). `stash@{0}` does not mean "mine"; it means "whatever anyone pushed most recently". Two interleaved ledger pushes:

    A: stash push  -> stash@{0} = A's rows
    B: stash push  -> stash@{0} = B's rows, A's slides to stash@{1}
    A: stash pop   -> A applies B's rows into A's tree, and DROPS them
    B: stash pop   -> B takes whatever is on top now

which is exactly the observed state: session 034951b2's ledger rows as uncommitted modifications inside a third session's worktree, on no branch. Reproduced the shift mechanically in a scratch repo (push, peer push, `git stash list --format='%H %gd'` shows the first entry at stash@{1}).

The carve-out that allowed `git stash` here — task_branch's own comment, "an intentional, controlled carve-out for known-safe paths only" — reasoned carefully about WHICH PATHS were safe to stash and not at all about the stack being shared. The paths were fine; the namespace is repo-wide. GENERALISATION: when allowlisting an operation, check whether its ADDRESSING is per-tree or per-repo. `stash@{n}`, `refs/stash` and the index are all repo-wide under a worktree layout.

FIXED (144fa0e6): `stash_benign` returns the created entry's COMMIT SHA (resolved via `rev-parse stash@{0}` immediately after the push, while it is still ours); `pop_stash` takes that SHA, runs `git stash apply <sha>`, then re-resolves the positional name from `git stash list --format='%H %gd'` to drop exactly that entry — re-resolved because a peer may have shifted it down in between. Failure modes asymmetric by design: apply fails => do NOT drop (losing a restore is recoverable, dropping someone else's rows is not); SHA unresolvable => return None, log ERROR with the grep-able stash message, restore nothing; no handle at the call site => restore nothing. Never falls back to stash@{0}. Pinned by TestSharedStackIsNotOurs (6 cases incl. "a peer pushed on top => drop must target stash@{1}") plus apply-by-SHA / no-`pop` assertions in test_ledger_push.py and test_task_branch.py. Doc'd at KB § PATTERNS/architect/branch-tree-tracking.md § 7.

RESIDUAL, NOT ATTEMPTED: the ledger append is not atomic — a row lives as an uncommitted modification before its commit, and that window is what made it stashable at all. A write -> commit -> push unit would remove the class rather than make it survivable. That is the s4-keeper move; this slice only makes the collision non-destructive.
task_branch action=start wire_env=True returns the full `wired` symlink list (3749 entries, 1.16M chars) in the MCP result, overflowing the agent's tool-output limit; return a count + sample instead.

available_ports(worktree_path=<wt>) ignored the worktree's start.sh: returned 8015/8190 as free while the worktree start.sh already registered academia-de-reciclagem on them (2026-09-14). Port resolution must honor worktree_path.

absorption_log and auto_improvement_log MCP tools have no worktree_path and resolve the ledger from the MCP server's startup REPO_ROOT (the primary checkout on dev) — calling them during self-branched work writes on dev, violating self-branching-mode. Add worktree_path like scaffold_product/task_branch.

scaffold_product llm_rewrite of README.md and MASTER-PROMPT.md returned None twice in a row (academia-de-reciclagem, agents; 2026-09-12/14), leaving seed-template prose; surface the underlying LLM error instead of a bare None.

scaffold_product emits a frontend without package-lock.json and without node_modules, while every product commits a lockfile (check_product_lockfile_dep_sync) — first vite build fails 'Cannot find module tailwindcss' (npx then resolves a stray ~/node_modules vite). Also task_branch wire_env only wires products that exist at start, so products scaffolded later in the worktree are unwired. Observed for academia-de-reciclagem + agents 2026-09-14; fix: scaffold runs npm install (or copies+renames the seed lockfile) and re-wires the worktree env.

Recurrence N=4 of the no-worktree_path writer class: absorption_log, auto_improvement_log, refresh_dependabot_coverage, refresh_ci_matrix_coverage all resolve REPO_ROOT from the MCP server's startup checkout (primary on dev), so an agent following self-branching-mode cannot use them from its worktree without writing on dev. N>=3 ⇒ formalize: a shared worktree_path param (or a keeper that every writer MCP tool accepts worktree_path), like scaffold_product/task_branch/vite_build already do. Observed 2026-09-14.

engineer_brief_compose emits the SAME hardcoded Acceptance block in every brief — the acceptance criteria of engineer_brief_compose ITSELF ('MCP tool noctus.dev.engineer_brief_compose returns the dict', 'CLI --compose-brief works', 'test_agent_kb_alignment still pass') — regardless of the slice. Observed on 5 of 5 briefs composed 2026-09-14 (seed token scopes, ChatWindow seams, academia data layer, importer, agents data layer). A brief dispatched as-is gives the engineer a wrong, unrelated done-definition. Also 'KB embeddings cache empty or embedding provider unreachable' degraded kb_references to [] on all 5. Fix: derive acceptance from a caller-supplied acceptance list (required arg) or from the target files' test roots; never a fixed template.

Keeper candidate: no detector catches a SECURITY DEFINER function left with PostgreSQL's default EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC grant. compliance.py only checks the search_path pin on SECURITY DEFINER (Supabase advisor 0011 shape). Caught by hand in G1 review 2026-09-14: agents.create_persona_version(p_org_id, ...) took the org as a parameter, checked no caller org/role, and had no REVOKE — callable by anon/authenticated via PostgREST /rpc for ANY org if the schema is exposed, i.e. prompt injection into an agent persona. House idiom already exists (social_wiring 027: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role; core 035 and erp 026 do the same for RLS helpers), so the rule is known but unenforced. Proposed keeper: every `SECURITY DEFINER` function in products/*/backend/migrations must be followed by a REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC for the same signature AND an explicit GRANT EXECUTE naming its intended roles (flag GRANT to anon/authenticated unless the body references auth.uid()/current_org_id() as a caller guard). Also worth a live-DB sweep of existing products for SECURITY DEFINER functions still executable by PUBLIC.

Recurrence N=2 → triage: the content secret scan (known token patterns pk_/sk-/ghp_/AKIA/-----BEGIN + Shannon-entropy threshold, returns the offending PATH never the value) now exists twice by construction — products/academia-de-reciclagem/backend/app/importer/secrets.py::scan_content and mcp/noctusai/tools/noctus/dev/knowledge_bundle_export.py::_content_has_secret — because the toolkit cannot import product app code. Both CAN import noctusai_lib (seed lib is an editable dep of the toolkit and a runtime dep of every product). Verdict: FORMALIZE now rather than wait for N=3 — a secret scanner that drifts between the export side and the import side silently lets a bundle the importer would refuse be written, or vice versa. Destination: noctusai_lib.security.secrets_scan (pure function + tests in mcp/noctusai/tests so CI runs them), both call sites import it; land with wave 1b academia API (which mounts POST /api/import).

session_end_sweep auto-heal flipped feat/academia-api-routes to status=shipped BEFORE the branch had any commit: branch tip == base, so an ancestry check ('tip is an ancestor of origin/dev') trivially passed. Observed 2026-09-14 by the A1b engineer, who corrected the row manually. A pointer auto-heal must require tip != base (the branch carries at least one commit) AND the tip reachable from origin/dev, otherwise every freshly-started worktree reads as integrated and a peer's collision planner treats the live claim as released.

branch_pointer writes the ledger row into the CALLER's worktree project-history/*.ndjson but commits and pushes via the primary checkout, so the worktree copy is left dirty and divergent orphan chore(branch-pointer) commits accumulate in the shared object store. Observed 2026-09-14 (A1b engineer folded the dirty ledger files into its feature commit; SEED-1's worktree carried a concurrent session's sweep rows). N>=3 in this session alone (SEED-1 foreign rows, A2 salvage row pushed by a peer's push, A1b folded rows). Fix: the tool must write, commit and push the ledger in ONE place (the primary or a dedicated ledger worktree) and never touch the caller's working tree; pairs with the 2026-09-09 atomic write->commit->push residual.

EVIDENCE for the 2026-09-14 tip==base auto-heal entry: a single session_end_sweep run at 2026-09-14T12:16:42 wrote 6 branch-pointer rows (+6 mirror rows) flipping feat/agents-api-routes, feat/social-wiring-agents-bridge, feat/academia-api-routes, feat/agents-ui, feat/academia-mcp-http-client and feat/academia-importer to status=shipped — four of them were live, in-progress engineer branches at that moment. The rows landed as dirty files inside the A1b worktree and the engineer folded them into the feature commit; had they merged, the global branch-tree map would report live branches as released and a peer's paths_overlap planner would treat their collision zones as free. The tech-lead removed them from the commit at integration (kept only the truthful salvage record) — this is a data-loss-adjacent failure mode, raising priority of the fix.

Recurrence N=2 → triage: every product that mounts ApiTokenAuditMiddleware needs a module-level lazy proxy (academia `_LazyAuditWriter`, social-wiring `LazyApiTokenAuditWriter`) because the middleware is registered at import time while the admin client / sqlite backend is only known lazily. The proxy is 3 lines each and identical in shape. Verdict today: keep product-local (thin, no logic), named destination = the seed middleware accepts `audit_writer_factory: Callable[[], ApiTokenAuditWriter]` (resolved once on first request) so products pass `lambda: make_api_token_audit_writer(admin, schema=...)` and no proxy class exists. MUST formalize at N=3 (the agents product is the likely third consumer if it ever accepts product tokens).

test_seam_guard (PreToolUse) scans the WHOLE post-edit test file, so a PRE-EXISTING unittest.mock.patch elsewhere in the file blocks ANY edit to it (seen: seed/lib/backend/tests/integrations/documents/test_extractor.py, classify_pdf_text_layer patches). Effect: a legacy violation makes the file un-editable, pushing engineers to put tests in a sibling file instead of fixing the debt. Guard should diff-scope new violations (or require fix-on-contact of the pre-existing patch with a clear message) rather than refuse the edit outright.

A seed-only commit prints fleet-wide [info] unbounded-PostgREST findings for products/therapy-platform (and similar unrelated products), burying the lines relevant to the staged change (the docx_render commit produced 670KB of hook output). Scope informational keeper output to staged paths, or summarize unrelated-product info findings as a count.

Brief-authoring slip (tech-lead, contract S-a): brief asserted a DB CHECK to match in 097 (none exists; estado_civil is deliberately unconstrained TEXT) and an 'identity extraction prompt' (the seed identity pipeline is regex/label parsers, no LLM prompt). Engineer correctly verified against the tree and adapted. Before briefing a seam, open the file that owns it — verify the mechanism shape (prompt vs parser, constraint vs free text) instead of inferring it from an audit summary.

Ledger-commit race on the PRIMARY checkout index (N=3 in one day): branch_pointer pushes, task_branch cleanup salvage rows and ledger drains all `git add`/commit in the shared primary checkout, so parallel engineers + the tech-lead collide on .git/index.lock ("salvage row committed locally but NOT pushed"; engineer S-a's pointer push blocked; the pre-crash session hit the same lock during overlapping teardowns). Also a dirty auto-improvement.ndjson in the primary makes the salvage rebase refuse ("unstaged changes"). Fix at the root: serialize primary ledger writes behind one lock-aware writer (retry-with-backoff on index.lock) or write ledger rows via a dedicated throwaway worktree instead of the shared primary index.

description: predeploy_check returns a confident verdict for whatever tree it is pointed at, without ever asserting that the tree is a sane thing to measure. Two failures inside twenty minutes on 2026-09-16, both from the same root: (1) noctusai-cd got three 'ready' verdicts computed against the PRIMARY checkout while it was 40 commits behind origin/dev with two dirty files, and only caught it by accident before blessing; (2) noctusai-c3 reported 'core 045 is not on dev' from the same stale primary tree, a wrong fact asserted confidently to two sessions. A sibling shape hit me minutes later: run against a freshly created worktree, predeploy_check reports status='blocked' on frontend_build with a raw ESM resolver stack trace, when the real cause is simply that node_modules was never installed there — an environment gap reported as a product defect. Suggested fix, all three legs: (a) refuse (or loudly downgrade to 'unverifiable') when the measured tree is behind its upstream or dirty, naming the sha it actually measured in the result; (b) echo the resolved tree + sha in every result so a verdict can never be quoted without its provenance; (c) classify 'node_modules absent' as its own named cause instead of an unknown frontend_build failure.

resolve_when: predeploy_check refuses or returns 'unverifiable' for a stale/dirty tree AND every result carries the measured sha

description: A SKIPPED predeploy check reports ok:true, so at the call site it is indistinguishable from a passed one. When no prod env snapshot resolves (no explicit prod_env_path, NOCTUS_PROD_ENV_FILE unset, no .env.prod/.env.production in the measured tree), the three prod-env legs — prod_config_parity, required_prod_env_present, cors_roster_complete — skip but still appear as {"check": ..., "ok": true} in the result, and status becomes "ready". The docstrings say it "SKIPs loudly", but the loudness never reaches the structured result a caller reads. Observed 2026-09-16: my two "ready" verdicts for academia-de-reciclagem and agents had verified only framework_deps, frontend_build, backend_tests and deploy_local_gitignored; noctusai-cd's three "ready" verdicts for social-wiring/seed/core were computed the same way, so social-wiring's env parity was never measured on the night of its deploy either. The live VPS .env in fact had NO PRODUCT_URL key for either of my slugs — precisely what cors_roster_complete exists to catch — and the tool still said ready. Fix: a skipped leg must be its own state in the result (e.g. ok:null / "skipped": true with the reason), status must never be "ready" while any leg is unmeasured (use "partial"/"unverifiable"), and the result should name which legs actually ran. This is the second false-green in the same tool and arguably the worse one: the stale-tree bug measures the wrong thing, this one reports having measured something it never touched.
source_ref: project-history/roadmaps/julia-agents-academia-2026-09.md — 2026-09-16 cutover (noctusai-36; confirmed by noctusai-cd against its own social-wiring deploy verdicts)
resolve_when: a skipped leg is distinguishable from a passed leg in predeploy_check's structured result AND status is never 'ready' with an unmeasured leg

description: deploy_verify's build_relevant_files list truncates at 20 entries without saying it truncated, so the evidence for a drift verdict can be entirely absent from the evidence it prints. Found by noctusai-c3 and confirmed by noctusai-cd on 2026-09-16: core and seed were reported as drift_detected, and the only paths that actually justified the verdict were 13 seed/ files — all of them cut off behind 20 agents-own paths (Dockerfile, app/runtime/*, secc/*) that do not trigger drift for core or seed at all. An operator reading the output sees a drift verdict whose listed causes cannot cause it, which invites exactly the wrong conclusion (either "this verdict is wrong, ignore it" or "the agents product broke core"). Fix: report the total count and mark the list as truncated (e.g. "showing 20 of 33"), and prefer the paths that DROVE the verdict over lexical order — the justifying files should be the ones that survive truncation, not the ones that happen to sort first.

description: The seed's 001 does `GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES ... TO anon` AND `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon`, so every table a product ever adds inherits full anon privileges automatically. Product schemas are PostgREST-exposed, so the ONLY thing protecting a new table is remembering to ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus not writing a permissive anon policy. community's 006 got that wrong (anon INSERT with WITH CHECK (true) on aplicacoes: anyone could insert a pre-approved application via /rest/v1, skipping validation and rate limits) and needed 007 to undo it; verified live with anon probes before and after. Root fix belongs in the seed: least-privilege per-table grants instead of the blanket grant + default privileges, and/or a keeper asserting relrowsecurity for every table in a product schema. The per-product revokes (community 007/008) are symptom patches.

(2) ResourceManager has no seam for managing a SUB-resource on a different endpoint (community's per-plan gateway refs): the engineer had to fall back to a bespoke row-action dialog. N=1 for the seam, so accepted for now, but a second product needing the same shape should get a real `secondaryActions`/nested-resource slot rather than a second bespoke dialog. Also logged from the same pass: `Intl.NumberFormat('pt-BR',{currency:'BRL'})` is hand-rolled in 6+ places fleet-wide (adconnect x7, core x2, seed/lib x2) while `@noctusai/lib`'s canonical `formatCurrency` already exists — N>=3, worth a sweep pointing those call sites at the canonical helper.

Confirmed against the real installed `stripe` SDK (v15.0.1, not the sys.modules dict-double `test_stripe_gateway.py` substitutes): a genuine `stripe.Customer`/`stripe.Subscription` object returned by the real SDK is a `StripeObject` subclass supporting `in`/`[]` but NOT `.get()` — calling `.get(...)` on it raises `AttributeError`. `real_stripe.py`'s `ensure_customer` (`found.get("email")`, `found.get("name")`) and `_to_gateway_subscription` (`sub.get("latest_invoice")`, `sub.get("metadata")`, `sub.get("current_period_end")`) all use this pattern, so every StripePaymentGateway method that touches a returned object would crash with AttributeError against a REAL Stripe key in production — the existing test suite never catches this because it substitutes `stripe` with a module whose Customer/Subscription/Charge doubles return plain dicts. Discovered while writing seed-payments-checkout-webhooks/webhook_events.py's real-signed-payload tests (parse_webhook_event's Stripe branch hit the identical shape via a genuine stripe.Webhook.construct_event() result and needed a `key in obj else default` helper instead of `.get()`). Out of scope to fix directly — real_stripe.py is off-limits per this dispatch's brief (peer branch feat/ef-r2-billing is concurrently consuming/extending the same package). Fix is likely: replace every `.get(...)` call on a Stripe SDK return value with `obj[key] if key in obj else default`, or convert via `obj.to_dict()` once at the top of each method.

The new live-pointer removal guard (b297ad6b) is defeated by session_end_sweep's auto-heal. Verified 2026-09-17: feat/ef-w8-models-worker's latest pointer row reads status=shipped with notes 'auto-healed by session_end_sweep: branch integrated into dev', while the peer session's worktree is still present and in use. Because 'shipped' is terminal, pointer_blocks_removal() returns False and the worktree is listed as stale/removable — the exact class of loss the guard was written to stop (2 engineers' work destroyed earlier the same day). Two candidate fixes: (a) the age guard must not be force-overridable when a worktree's mtime is recent, i.e. treat recent filesystem activity as liveness independent of the ledger; (b) session_end_sweep must not flip a pointer to a terminal status while the worktree directory still exists — auto-heal should write a distinct status (e.g. 'integrated-worktree-live') that the sweep still treats as blocking. Preferred: (b) plus (a) as defence in depth, since the ledger is a claim and the filesystem is evidence. Also note the guard fails OPEN when the pointer query returns nothing.

CLASSIFICATION BUG with real data loss. BENIGN_REFRESH_PATTERNS includes `project-history/*.ndjson`, so task_branch's auto-stash treats the append-only LEDGERS (branch-tree, auto-improvement, worktree-salvage, vector-costs, and the branch-tree mirror) as disposable hook side-effects. They are both: usually regenerated noise, but also the durable rows agents append. Verified 2026-09-17: 7 stash entries held 25 ledger rows that had never reached dev, including a tech-lead auto-improvement drift row; a peer session recovered them to dev in 3789fefc before dropping the entries, and archived the dropped stashes at refs/stash-archive/<sha>. Without that recovery the rows were gone. Fix: for `project-history/*.ndjson` do NOT stash — write a `chore(ledger)` WIP commit instead. These files are `merge=union` in .gitattributes precisely because they are append-only, so a commit is always safe to rebase and can never conflict destructively, whereas a stash is a silent holding area that a later drop deletes. Keep .claude/cache/* and the regenerated kb-counts docs as stashable (they are genuinely derived and reproducible). This is the FOURTH member of today's shared-state family: tools trusting a written claim about shared state (merged flag, pointer status, benign label) instead of checking the state itself.

A "hold dev pushes" freeze is NOT expressible today, and the reason is an invisible side effect: `task_branch action='start'` pushes a branch-pointer row to dev. The verb reads as "create a worktree", so an orchestrator that has accepted a freeze can honour it in intent and still break it by dispatching. Verified 2026-09-17: I accepted a peer's release freeze, dispatched 3 slices, and the pointer rows from `start` (95f84225, f2b516a5) cancelled their in-flight CI run TWICE — the second time after 44/45 jobs were already green. Costly because a cancelled CI run on the exact sha is a bless prerequisite. Same shape as the claim-vs-evidence family, one layer out: the caller cannot see the shared-state write from the call site. Proposed fix, in order: (a) `start` accepts `push_dev=False`; (b) a repo freeze marker (e.g. project-history/freeze.json with holder, reason, expiry) that `start`, `branch_pointer` and the ledger drains consult and refuse against, naming the holder in the refusal — a freeze becomes STATE, not an etiquette agreement between sessions; (c) `release stage='bless'` sets and clears it automatically, since bless is exactly when a freeze is needed. Peer (noctusai-5d) agrees and asked me to take it after module 3. [RE-LOGGED 2026-09-17: the original row (ts 04:14:22) was discarded by a `git reset --hard origin/dev` that re-synced a diverged primary; the reset was the guard's own sanctioned repair and the row was recovered from a pre-reset patch.]

primary_write_guard's `cp` handling is a real parser bug, and its refusal message mis-teaches the fix. `_ALWAYS_WRITE` resolves EVERY path-looking arg as a write target, so `cp <primary-file> <scratchpad-dest>` is refused on the SOURCE — but cp READS arg 1 and WRITES the last, so a pure read-out-of-primary is denied. Same defect applies to `install`, `rsync` and `ln` (dest-only semantics); `mv` is correctly all-args since it also removes the source. Suggested fix: for the dest-only set, target = the `-t`/`--target-directory` value when present, else the LAST path positional, with sources treated as reads; keep the conservative all-args + uncertain fallback when there are <2 positionals or any token is unexpandable. Verified same session: a `cat <primary-file> > <scratchpad-dest>` redirect IS correctly allowed, which proves the redirect leg is right and only the positional leg is wrong. SECOND observation, and the more important one: the guard ALREADY has the designed repair for a diverged primary — `_is_sync_to_remote_git` permits `git reset --hard <remote-tracking-ref>` for exactly this state — but its refusal message only ever names `task_branch`, so an agent hitting the wall on `git reset`/`git stash`/`rm` is never told the one command that works. I concluded the deadlock was closed and was about to escalate to the user before reading the module and finding the exemption. Suggested fix: when ctx shows the primary DIVERGED from its upstream, the refusal should name `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` as the remedy. A gate whose escape hatch exists but is undiscoverable from its own refusal is functionally a gate without one. NOTE: `git reset -- <ledger-path>` is still refused although `git restore -- <ledger-path>` is exempt via `_is_ledger_only_git` — the 2026-08-27 'a ledger may be dirtied but not cleaned' asymmetry was fixed for restore/checkout and `reset` was overlooked; it is the index-side twin and belongs in the same exemption.

The whatsapp package's __init__ re-export eagerly pulls the ENTIRE supabase family (supabase + postgrest + gotrue, ~50 modules) because it re-exports `connection_store`, which constructs a Supabase-backed store. Verified on the promoted tip 063ac09d: `import noctusai_lib.integrations.whatsapp` leaves 50 supabase-family entries in sys.modules. This broke `mcp/meta` and `mcp/olx` at import time (the local `mcp/supabase/` directory SHADOWS the installed `supabase` package there), and was fixed in 063ac09d by making `api_keys` resolve credentials lazily — one layer ABOVE the cause. The eager re-export itself is untouched, so any future consumer importing `integrations.whatsapp` in an environment where `supabase` is shadowed or absent breaks the same way; N=2 already (meta, olx). This also contradicts the seed's own stated pattern next door in `seed/framework/backend/noctusai_seed/routers.py`, which deliberately defers the WhatsApp connector import with the comment "keeps the WhatsApp connector import cost off the hot path for products without a WhatsApp chatbot" — the __init__ re-export re-imposes exactly that cost on every consumer, including ones that never touch connections. Root fix: make the `connection_store` re-export lazy in `__init__` (module-level `__getattr__`, PEP 562) or drop it from `__all__` so consumers import the submodule explicitly, keeping the supabase dependency off the import path of anything that only wants the WAHA client / mappers / rate_limit. NOT shipped now: prod boot is unaffected (products have supabase installed and the import succeeds, RC=0), and changing seed/ re-widens the fleet build scope mid-release. Queue for the next seed slice.

🔴 RETRACTION of the entry logged 2026-09-17T17:54:47Z against this same target. That entry claimed (a) the eager supabase import is "still live" on the promoted tip and (b) its cause is the `connection_store` re-export in this __init__. BOTH CLAIMS ARE FALSE. Ground truth: commit 063ac09d ALREADY fixed it completely, at the correct level — it replaced an eager `from noctusai_lib.config.credentials import resolve_credential` in `security/api_keys.py` with a call-time lazy proxy. The real chain is `config.credentials` → `integrations.database` → supabase client, and api_keys is the single seam every re-export path (security, connection_store, integrations.whatsapp) funnels through, so one lazy proxy covers all of them. Verified empirically on the fixed tree: `import noctusai_lib.integrations.whatsapp` leaves ZERO supabase/postgrest/gotrue modules in sys.modules, and probing all 12 whatsapp submodules plus the token_store/api_keys chain individually shows none introducing supabase. My "50 supabase-family modules" measurement was taken while the PRIMARY CHECKOUT sat at 3cdf7414 — one commit BEFORE the fix — because I had pulled to 3cdf7414 earlier and never re-pulled before probing. HOW THIS HAPPENED, and the reason it is worth a ledger row rather than a silent delete: this is the stale-primary class recorded in memory `feedback_stale_primary_poisons_local_reading_gates` the SAME DAY, where spa_smoke's roster and deploy_verify's port both misreported off a stale local checkout. I wrote that memory and then reproduced the failure a third time, in a worse form — a stale read became a confident public claim that a peer's correct fix was defective, which risked them re-fixing an already-fixed thing. THE GENERALISABLE RULE: `git rev-parse HEAD` before any measurement whose conclusion is about code that is live, and state the sha measured alongside the result. A measured number carries no date; the checkout does. Also: I nearly shipped a redundant PEP 562 refactor of this __init__ off that false premise, and only caught it by tracing the import chain empirically instead of trusting my own earlier reading — the intended "root fix" (lazy-export connection_store here) would have been dead code addressing a path that no longer pulls supabase. No code change is needed in this file; the task branch feat/seed-whatsapp-lazy-connection-store-export is being removed unused.

Item 3 follow-up decision (2026-09-17/18, cache-scoping-and-gate-integrity slice): task_branch's wire_env=False default was a "separately defaulted in two places, drifted apart" bug — the pure task_branch() signature and the register() MCP wrapper each carried their own default, and nothing enforced parity. Shipped targeted regression tests asserting BOTH default to True (test_task_branch.py::TestWireEnvDefaultCannotSilentlyRegress). Considered a GENERAL keeper (check_mcp_wrapper_default_parity: AST-derive every register()-nested @server.tool wrapper, resolve the pure function it delegates to, flag any shared-param default mismatch) for the class more broadly. Ran a bounded read-only survey first (137 files, 213 wrapper/pure-fn pairs) rather than shipping blind: found 7 pre-existing mismatches (branch_pointer.notes None-vs-'', cost_evaluation.extensions None-vs-DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS, prod_consent.{slug,session_id,consent_ref,worktree_path} ''-vs-None, tunnel_config.worktree_path ''-vs-None) — all benign empty-string/None sentinel differences, NONE a true/false safety-flag flip. DECISION: do not ship the general keeper in this slice — it would need a deliberate allowlist for these 7 known-benign cases to avoid immediate false-positive noise on unrelated tools, and building+calibrating that correctly is a separate scoped project, not a same-slice add (shipping it uncalibrated is itself the 'gate blind to its own false positives' anti-pattern this session is closing). Recommend: a follow-up project that either (a) aligns the 7 mismatches to a single sentinel convention then ships the keeper strict, or (b) ships the keeper with those 7 as a documented, reasoned baseline (mirrors the validate_schema=False baseline pattern in compliance-regression-baseline.md).

Second-order finding while fixing the auto-improvement cross-tree refresh/check parity bug (2026-09-17/18, cache-scoping-and-gate-integrity slice): `absorption_tracking.py` has the SAME structural precondition (its `LEDGER_PATH` is `settings.LEDGER_ROOT`-pinned, deliberately unwrapping the worktree boundary back to primary) as auto-improvement did, feeding `check_absorptions_cache_freshness` (severity warning, non-blocking). WORSE than auto-improvement was: (a) `absorption_tracking.refresh()` has NO `worktree_path` parameter at all (only a raw `ledger: Path | None`) — no escape hatch exists yet to add threading to; (b) `cli.py` has NO `--refresh-absorptions-cache` flag at all, despite the keeper's own docstring claiming `python mcp/noctusai/cli.py --refresh-absorptions-cache` as the remediation — a documented remedy that does not exist as a command. Not fixed in this slice (advisory/non-blocking, and needs new plumbing — a parameter add + a CLI flag add + tests — rather than the one-line threading fix that closed the auto-improvement instance). Recommended follow-up: add `worktree_path: str | None` to `absorption_tracking.refresh()` mirroring `auto_improvement._ledger_path_for`, add the missing `--refresh-absorptions-cache` CLI flag (threading `--worktree-path`), and a regression test in the shape of `test_cli_worktree_path.py::test_refresh_then_check_agree_on_the_same_worktree`. General rule + full inventory recorded in `KB § PATTERNS/common/cache-auto-freshness.md` § Cross-tree refresh/check source-parity.

Spec-vs-code drift can be laundered into "intended design" by the doc that is supposed to catch it. Found 2026-09-21: f5-template-spec.md §2.17/§5.1 already specified the contract's witness block as NOME+E-MAIL+RG with "nome+rg" hard-required, but contrato_gerador's template/context/gate had drifted to print and REQUIRE a CPF instead — and CONTRACT-FIELD-PROVENANCE-MAP.md had then written that drift down as the answered [Q14] design.
