description: A per-org capability switch is only real if EVERY consumer reads it — and the one that skipped it was invisible for 4 days. Found 2026-09-21: the org set llm_vision_provider='anthropic' on 2026-09-17 with a valid anthropic key, yet card_hub identity extraction and imovel_hub matricula extraction kept calling OpenAI (zero credits) and burning documents to extracao_status='erro'. matriculas and certidoes in the SAME product already consumed resolve_vision_provider correctly, so the setting LOOKED wired. Three compounding reasons it stayed hidden: (1) the failing chain ended in a class literally named OpenAIMediaResolver, so "it calls OpenAI" read as intended rather than as a bug; (2) the lib HAD a credit_probe organ that classifies insufficient_quota distinctly, but only edicao_fotos and the settings key-tester consume it — the extraction path just wrote the raw vendor 429 string into a DB column nobody surfaces; (3) extraction is a detached BackgroundTask, so the operator's upload returned 201 and the failure surfaced nowhere in the UI. Lesson: when adding a per-org provider switch, the unit of work is not "add the setting" but "enumerate every call site of the capability and prove each reads it" — and a vendor-named adapter class is a smell that the seam was never meant to be switchable. Detector idea: flag any module that constructs a vision/chat adapter without a resolve_*_provider call in the same function.

"Route exists and the page renders" hid four independent silent-failure modes on one card. Live prod UI probe 2026-09-21 of the card-hub contract flow surfaced, in one sitting: (1) a Nova-parcela 422 swallowed whole — forma_pagamento is max_length=50 server-side, the input has no maxLength/counter/error surface, so Salvar is a permanent no-op with nothing in the console; (2) criar_parcela writes every row ordem=0 while the contract numbers them "Parcela 01/02/03"; (3) the Completude panel prints raw rule keys (parcelas_nao_cobrem_valor_negociado) though the generator's own readiness panel already has human rotulo+destino text for exactly these; (4) a parcela picker rendering raw floats (100000.0) beside a currency-formatted table. None of these are caught by scan_wiring (route exists, data renders) or by the test suite (each side is individually correct). The common shape: a backend constraint or derived value that the FE never learned about. Lesson: wiring-audit should include a "constraint parity" leg — for every write form, assert the FE mirrors the Pydantic field caps and renders ApiError.details, because a swallowed 422 is indistinguishable from a dead button to the operator. Detector idea: AST-diff StrictHttpModel Field(max_length=...) against the corresponding FE input's maxLength.

Two deploy-chain tools returned verdicts that described the APPARATUS, not the subject — and unlike the other 5 instances of this class on 2026-09-20, these did NOT announce themselves as reds. (1) `deploy_image` returned `status='up_to_date'`, `exit_code=0`, "image == running image; no redeploy needed" while the GHCR fleet build for the CURRENT prod sha (7dcf0285) was still `in_progress`. The running image genuinely equalled the latest PUBLISHED image because the new one did not exist yet. Taken at face value this reads as "deploy complete" and would have produced a confident verification of a deploy that never happened. Fix: `deploy_image` knows the prod sha; when the latest published image predates it AND a build for that sha is in flight, the verdict must be `inconclusive`/`build_pending`, never `up_to_date` with exit 0. (2) `release stage='promote'` returned `status='error'`, `exit_code=1` with "promote push to prod failed: ! [remote rejected] cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/prod': is at 7dcf02856 but expected c9edef8f34" — i.e. a compare-and-swap rejection whose ACTUAL value equalled the INTENDED target. The push had already landed (`snapshot_done: true`, verified independently via `git ls-remote`: prod=7dcf0285, prod-backup=c9edef8f, exactly as planned). This is the most dangerous shape found all day: the documented response to a failed promote is to ROLL BACK to prod-backup, so acting on this false red would have reverted a correct, completed production deploy. Fix: a CAS rejection whose remote value == the target sha is an idempotent no-op and MUST be reported as success. Both belong as signatures in the shared harness-validity table built on feat/harness-validity-everywhere (9288a348).

target: products/core (public schema) + products/seed — anon grant lockdown coverage gap
description: The 2026-09-20 anon-grant lockdown slice (commits b5abd189/3315762c) scoped itself to "the 9 schemas that inherit templates/product-seed/backend/migrations/001_seed.sql" and shipped forward-only REVOKE migrations for each. That scope was derived from TEMPLATE PROPAGATION, and it structurally misses two LIVE schemas that carry the identical trap: (a) `public` — the platform schema, 30 tables (orgs, users, licenses, plans), 29 anon-readable, with `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... anon=arwdDxtm` registered by TWO grantors (`postgres` AND `supabase_admin`); (b) `seed` — live, 3 of 4 tables anon-readable. Verified live 2026-09-21 after the 4 live product schemas were disarmed: social_wiring/academia_de_reciclagem/agents/community all show `anon` absent from default table privileges, while public and seed still show 🔴 ARMED. NOTHING IS EXPOSED TODAY (`exposed = 0` fleet-wide — every table has RLS), so this is the latent trap, not a live hole: the next table created in `public` or `seed` inherits anon access and is exposed until someone remembers RLS, which is exactly how the 4 `_*_backup_20260902` tables (21,567 rows of PII) happened. NOT fixed in-session for two deliberate reasons: no migration exists so it would mean hand-writing DDL against the platform schema in prod, and `public` shares a default ACL with `supabase_admin` (Supabase-managed), so the blast radius reaches their tooling. Also still armed and correctly untouched: 5 inactive product schemas (adconnect, daily_life, igig, orbity, p_studio — the catalog working-scope rule refuses them, they must be fixed BEFORE reactivation) and 4 auxiliary schemas with no product migration path at all (imobi_scheduling, mailing, media_scheduling, pilates). Recommended: one slice covering public+seed, and a reactivation-gate for the other 9.

A NOC-REMEDIATE marker enumerated its call sites and UNDER-counted them — the marker's own list became the fix's blind spot. 2026-09-21: the marker NOC-REMEDIATE[identity-extractor-factory-ignores-tipo-documento] named two callers of extrair_identidade (the upload route, the recovery sweep). By the time the fix was dispatched, a THIRD caller existed — reextrair_documento_route, added hours earlier on a parallel branch — carrying the identical bug. An engineer working strictly to the marker would have removed it while leaving the newest path broken, which is worse than not fixing it: the marker is gone, the class no longer shows in scan_remediation_markers, and the truncation silently returns on every retry. The engineer caught it only by grepping for the call shape rather than trusting the list. Lesson: a marker may name an EXAMPLE call site but must never be read as an exhaustive inventory — the fixer's first step is to re-derive the caller set from the code, and the marker's removal is only honest once that re-derived set is fully covered. Detector idea: when a NOC-REMEDIATE class is removed, require the commit to show every call site of the named symbol was touched, not just the ones the marker listed.
source_ref: commit e8a716c1 vs marker written in 883e3ab0

description: Auto-pushed ledger commits repeatedly cancel the CI run that is gating a prod deploy. Observed 2026-09-21: integrating four branches in sequence produced, after each integrate, a `chore(ledger): ship the append-only ledger rows written this run` / `chore(cost-log): deliver session ledger churn [auto]` push. Each push cancelled the in-flight `Tests & Build` run for the previous commit via workflow concurrency. Four of the last six dev runs show `cancelled`, and the only `success` belongs to a ledger commit rather than to a code commit. The practical effect is that "CI-green before prod" — which CLAUDE.md makes MANDATORY because prod is first-contact for a running image — cannot be satisfied for the code commit itself; you end up green on a commit whose diff is an append-only ndjson row. Options worth weighing: exclude ledger-only paths from the Tests & Build trigger (they cannot affect the image), or batch the ledger drain to fire once at session end rather than per integrate, or make the concurrency group path-aware so a ledger push does not cancel a code run.

Worktree .env wiring is a false-green channel: a local suite can pass because task_branch symlinked the real credentials in, then fail in CI which has none. 2026-09-21: an engineer reported "4712 passed, 0 failed" for social-wiring, run correctly with a worktree-pinned PYTHONPATH. CI on the merged tip returned 8 failed / 4710 passed — every failure in that engineer's own new test file, every one `SupabaseException: supabase_url is required`. Cause: `noctus.dev.task_branch action='start'` wires ~4,600 env symlinks into the worktree including `.env`, so SUPABASE_URL was present locally; the new tests call a deps factory that now reaches resolve_credential → a Supabase client constructor. The engineer did nothing wrong procedurally — they verified the way the methodology told them to. The verdict channel itself is what lies: the environment that produces the local verdict is strictly richer than the one that gates the deploy. This belongs alongside the existing verdict-channel-integrity rule (a pipe returns tail's verdict; silence is not a pass) as a third shape: a RICHER environment returns a greener verdict than the gating one. Mitigation: engineer briefs should require at least one env-stripped run (`env -u SUPABASE_URL -u SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ...`) before claiming green, or dispatch-time guidance to unset the wired secrets for the final verification pass.
source_ref: CI run 35550988522 vs engineer report on commit e8a716c1

description: All 19 certidão consultations in prod are UNLINKED, so the contract generator cannot see a single one. Verified 2026-09-21: social_wiring.certidao_consultas has 19 rows, every one status='concluida', and every one with cliente_id IS NULL AND atendimento_parte_id IS NULL. The generator reads certidoes.service.certidoes_por_parte / certidoes_por_cliente, which filter on exactly those two columns — so a party can have a complete, paid-for certidão set and the readiness gate will still report all 12 as faltando. This is NOT a missing mechanism: POST /api/certidoes/consultas/{id}/vincular-parte and .../vincular-cliente both exist (migrations 107/116), CertidoesPartePanel.tsx exists, and useCertidoes.ts wires both. The gap is adoption/discoverability — the operator runs consultations from the standalone /certidoes page, where nothing prompts for or defaults the card linkage, and the link step is invisible from where the work actually happens. Worth deciding: should a consulta started from a card's Certidões panel auto-link, and should the standalone page surface an "unlinked" state the way the card surfaces "faltando"? Related: every consulta requests total_certidoes=10 but records concluidas of 6-9, while still reporting status='concluida' — a partial result presented as complete, which is its own no-silent-errors question.

Live extraction probe 2026-09-21 (Anthropic vision, image-only 3-page certidão de casamento) returned rg_orgao='COTIA/SP' for a document that contains NO RG at all. The fixture's only nearby text is "LOCAL: Cotia - SP"; the parser took the place name as an issuing organ and emitted a field the source never asserted, while leaving `rg` itself null — so the pair is internally incoherent (an orgão expedidor with no document number). Everything else on that read was exact: cpf [REDACTED-cpf], data_casamento [REDACTED-personal-date], data_emissao 2024-06-06, estado_civil 'divorciado' (correctly read off the page-3 averbação), regime_bens 'comunhao_parcial'. Two things worth fixing: (1) rg_orgao should never be emitted without an rg — an orphan orgão is evidence the parser matched geography, not an ID; (2) `nacionalidade` and `profissao` are present in the fixture's page 1 and were NOT extracted, and both are hard-required by the contract's qualification gate, so the operator still has to type them by hand even on a perfect read. This matters beyond tidiness: contract §5.2's whole premise is that extracted values are the truth, and a fabricated qualification field goes into a legal instrument.

A document filed under the wrong tipo_documento is unrecoverable: there is no reclassify path, so it can never be extracted. Found 2026-09-21 while trying to repair the live Rodrigo card. Its four identity PDFs were uploaded as tipo_documento='outro' (the old AnexosSection default), and `outro` is not in TIPOS_EXTRAIVEIS. The new POST .../documentos/{id}/extrair correctly refuses them with a 400 on tipo_documento — but documentos_service exposes no update/patch for tipo_documento at all (only upload, url, delete, reextrair, list_acessos), and the router has no PATCH on a documento. So the only recovery is delete + re-upload, which destroys the LGPD access history the whole cliente_documento_acessos table exists to preserve. The fix is not a trivial column update: tipo_documento carries categoria_lgpd AND drives retencao_ate via documento_retencao.dias_para, so a reclassify must recompute the retention date and should log the reclassification as its own access-log event with the before/after tipo — an operator saying "this is actually a certidão de casamento" is a data-category change, not a typo correction. Worth deciding deliberately rather than bolting on, because reclassifying INTO 'identidade' tightens retention while reclassifying OUT of it loosens it.

The vision rung is excellent on real cartório scans; the FIELD PARSER is what fails. Probed 2026-09-21 against the actual 2-page certidão de casamento on the live Rodrigo card (Anthropic, max_pages=None). The OCR text came back complete and accurate — 4611 chars covering both spouses' full names, both CPFs, both birth dates by extenso, filiação, matrícula, the regime, and the verso averbação verbatim: "através da ESCRITURA PÚBLICA de Divórcio Consensual, lavrada aos 08/07/2022 ... foi realizado o DIVÓRCIO CONSENSUAL do casal ROBERIO CASSEMIRO DOS SANTOS e REGINA MARIA PELOSI". From that text the extractor returned ONLY data_casamento, data_emissao, and a bogus rg_orgao='COTIA/SP'. Missing: nome, cpf, estado_civil, regime_bens, nacionalidade. Two concrete causes. (1) REGIME: the document says "SEPARAÇÃO ABSOLUTA DE BENS, CONFORME ESCRITURA DE PACTO ANTENUPCIAL" — _REGIME_BENS_PADROES matches SEPARACAO TOTAL|CONVENCIONAL|OBRIGATORIA|LEGAL but NOT ABSOLUTA, which is the standard cartório wording for separação convencional. (2) TWO-SPOUSE AMBIGUITY: a certidão de casamento names two people with equal prominence, and extrair_identidade writes to exactly ONE cliente — so nome/cpf cannot be chosen without knowing which spouse the document is being filed for. Declining may be the correct conservative behaviour, but then it should be a NAMED refusal the operator can see, not a silent empty field; and estado_civil/regime_bens apply to BOTH spouses and should still be extracted. Worth noting the same document also reveals a pacto antenupcial (Livro 659, pgs 002-004, 01/07/2011) which the contract's escritura_pacto/registro_pacto types exist to capture.

The funil's "Novo lead" dialog cannot name the person the lead is for. Verified live 2026-09-21: the dialog's complete field set is Data de entrada, Tipo, "Nome da marca" (the MARCA/brand, not the person), "Telefone ou email", Tier do anúncio, Origem, Corretor, Empreendimento, Região, Código do imóvel, Observações, Follow-up date + nota. There is no name input at all. Leads arriving from campaigns/portals carry a name in their payload, so the board looks fine in normal use — but a lead created by hand starts anonymous. This matters directly to contract automation: the card's titular cliente derives from the lead, and `nome_oficial` is the FIRST thing the contract qualification gate hard-requires for every party. It also means an operator cannot create a deal from a walk-in or a phone call without going somewhere else first. The "Cliente" label sitting above a "Nome da marca" placeholder is a second, smaller problem — in this product "cliente" means the person elsewhere (clientes table, /clientes page, cliente_id on every card), so the label and the placeholder disagree about what the field is.

A hand-created lead has no contract surface for up to 6 hours and an operator cannot speed it up. Verified live 2026-09-21: created a lead through the UI (/leads → Base de Leads → Novo lead) with a valid contato_norm. The funil auto-created its atendimento immediately — titulo='[REDACTED-phone]' (the phone, since the dialog cannot capture a name) — but with cliente_id NULL. Per the card-hub's own routing, a card with cliente_id NULL opens LeadDetailModal, not ClienteCardDialog, so there is NO Contratos subpage, no Negociação, no document intake: the entire contract pipeline is unreachable. cliente_id is attached only by clientes_backfill_job, whose interval defaults to 6h (config.clientes_backfill_interval_hours=6). There is a startup catch-up (added 2026-08-31 for exactly this class of starvation) but it only helps leads that existed BEFORE the restart. POST /api/clientes/backfill exists on the router but has no operator-facing surface anywhere in the UI — no button on /clientes, /clientes/revisao or the funil. The module's own docstring already names the consequence ("unmovable, because stage_gate refuses a card with no titular") for the scheduler-starvation case; this is the same dead end reached by simply creating a lead by hand. Worth either attaching the cliente synchronously on manual lead creation (the contato_norm is right there and fully resolvable) or exposing the existing backfill route as an operator action.

An anonymised fixture is a MODEL of the failure, not the failure — verify a fix against the real artifact before believing it. 2026-09-21: to avoid committing client PII I handed an engineer a hand-anonymised version of a real cartório certidão, faithful in structure and wording, and asked them to fix four parse defects. They fixed all four and reported green, including a genuine root cause (cartório "nada consta" disclaimers naming event categories only to negate them were being counted as events). But when I re-ran the REAL document's transcription against their branch, estado_civil was still None. My anonymised fixture had truncated the document's tail, and the tail was the trigger: every CNJ-format certidão ends with a "DETALHAMENTO DA MATRÍCULA" legend enumerating book types — "4. Livro C (Obito)" — which is neither an event nor a negation, so the new negation filter never saw it, yet it still counted as an ÓBITO occurrence and still collapsed a genuine DIVÓRCIO to nenhuma. The engineer had honestly flagged the risk in their own report ("that fixture's disclaimer happens not to name a conflicting category"), which is what prompted the re-test. Lesson: when PII forces a synthetic fixture, the fixture is a hypothesis about the failure and inherits the author's blind spots; the acceptance test must still run against the original artifact, even if only the tech-lead can hold it. Cheap mitigation used here: a parser-only A/B (no LLM, no cost) against the real transcription, which is also the only verification channel that survived both LLM providers running out of credit.

CLOSED (2026-09-21, commits 3e06a5d9 + 75a7acf1): the certidão parser dropped estado_civil on every CNJ-format certidão. Root cause was a document-structure problem, not a wording one. Every CNJ certidão (Provimento 63/2017) ends with a "DETALHAMENTO DA MATRÍCULA" appendix explaining the serial-number format by enumerating book types — "4. Livro C (Obito)". That is a numbered list item about NUMBERING, not an event and not a negation, so it survived the negation filter, yet the flat keyword scan counted it as an óbito occurrence. It then disagreed with the genuine DIVÓRCIO averbação in the same zone, len(eventos)>1, and the whole field collapsed to nenhuma. Fixed with two independent structural guards: clip the averbação zone at the appendix heading (every real averbação precedes it), plus a shape guard on the CNJ-regulated book-legend form `N. Livro X (...)` that holds even when the heading is mis-transcribed. Verified by tech-lead A/B on a reproduction of the real document, no LLM: dev (None,'nenhuma',None) → fix ('divorciado','alta','AVERBACAO: DIVORCIO'), with regime_bens ('separacao_total','alta') in the same run. Also landed alongside: rg_orgao can no longer be fabricated from a "Comarca de X/UF" jurisdiction nor travel without an rg; data_emissao can no longer be asserted from a birthdate sitting later in the text; a two-spouse certidão now returns a NAMED refusal (error='titulares_multiplos') instead of silently empty nome/cpf. Two NOC-REMEDIATE markers remain open: identity-extractor-disambiguation-hint and nacionalidade-identity-parser.

certidao_casamento is flagged identidade=false, so the single most contract-critical document sits under "Outros" in the new tipo picker. Observed live 2026-09-21 in prod: the picker groups IDENTIDADE (cnh, cpf, rg) first, then OUTROS — and "Certidão de casamento (com averbações) — estado civil e regime de bens" lands in OUTROS, below "Comprovante de endereço" and "Fotos do imóvel". Yet it is the ONLY document that carries estado_civil, regime_bens and data_casamento, all three hard-required by the contract qualification gate, and it IS in TIPOS_EXTRAIVEIS. The grouping is driven by cliente_documento_tipos.identidade, which migration 103 left false for certidao_casamento (and 110 did the same for certidao_nascimento) while 057/119 set it true for rg/cpf and 142 set it true for cnh. Same row also has retencao_dias NULL — flagged separately by the engineer who wrote 142 as a pre-existing retention gap, since categoria_lgpd='identidade' implies the 1825-day policy its siblings carry. Both are one forward migration. Also minor, same surface: the rg and cpf option labels read "qualificação civil (intake LGPD concluído 2026-09-16)" — internal provenance from the migration leaking into an operator-facing dropdown.
source_ref: live prod tipo picker, Rodrigo card, 2026-09-21

description: CORRECTION to two earlier entries in this ledger from 2026-09-21, both of which named the wrong mechanism. (1) I logged "the Novo lead dialog cannot capture the person's name". WRONG: leads.cliente_nome exists, is read by identidade_service.leads_row_to_source as the person's name, and feeds the card title via migration 034's spawn_funil_card trigger. There is no marca_id on leads at all. The actual defect was purely the FE label — the input read "Cliente" with placeholder "Nome da marca", so it presented as an ad-campaign brand field and operators left it blank, which is precisely why the prod lead I created carried cliente_nome NULL. Fixed as wording only (commit e0165794): "Nome do cliente" / "Nome completo do cliente", same binding, no schema or contract change. (2) I logged "a hand-created lead is unusable for up to 6 hours with no operator override", inferring the 6h clientes_backfill_interval_hours was the only attach path. WRONG: create_lead already scheduled clientes_backfill_job.run_now as a BackgroundTask, which attached within seconds — prod lead 53732b8f now carries cliente_id 94f3ec1b, identidade_incerta=false. I had queried the DB immediately after creation, seen NULL, and generalised from one early read. The real defect was narrower: the attach was ASYNCHRONOUS, so the 201 could return before the card was workable, and a fast operator hits a card with no titular that stage_gate refuses to move. Now synchronous inline before the response. Method lesson: a NULL read taken moments after a write proves nothing about steady state — re-read before inferring a missing mechanism, and grep for an existing BackgroundTask/sweep before concluding one does not exist.
source_ref: commit e0165794; prod lead 53732b8f / atendimento b2854c77

description: primary_write_guard has a hole at the MCP-tool layer: noctus.dev.organ_knowledge_append takes no worktree_path and wrote seed/lib/frontend/src/design-system/chat/ChatWindow.organ.yaml straight into the PRIMARY checkout on shared `dev` from a worktree-isolated engineer session (2026-09-21, julia-retry-after-countdown), also re-serializing the whole YAML. Bash/Edit/Write were correctly refused when the engineer tried to revert. Fix: give it (and sibling write tools lacking worktree_path) a worktree_path param mirroring register_organ, or refuse without one when REPO_ROOT is the primary on a shared branch. Same wrong-tree family as predeploy_check/tunnel_config/migrate_product (N>=5).

Documents extracted under older parser/classifier code keep their stale verdict forever: Rodrigo's CNH-e sat at sem_dados (rung-1 accepted the Serpro stamp) long after f9e93df5/cbdcd9a9 fixed the classifier, and two CNHs sat at erro (OpenAI 429) after the provider fix. Nothing re-runs them; only a human clicking the (off-screen) retry. Needs a versioned re-extraction sweep: stamp extractor version on the doc row and re-queue sem_dados/erro rows when the version moves.

error-vs-notice channel: a result that READ the document but withheld some fields must never ride `error` — consumers treat error as unreadable and discard the valid fields on the same result (two-spouse certidão lost estado civil/regime/datas). Fixed c6919e3d with IdentityFields.aviso + TitularEsperado hint. Generalizable rule for every seed extractor Protocol: failure channel vs notice channel are distinct fields.

UI findings from live e2e 2026-09-21: (1) a failed anexo's long error text pushes the 'Tentar ler novamente' button off-screen horizontally (row doesn't truncate/wrap); (2) checklist CPF row renders '—' with a checked box while clientes.cpf is set (Regina); (3) closed atendimentos (status aceita, e.g. Rodrigo's) are unreachable from the Funil search — no way to reopen the card to generate the contract from the funnel.

Shape-only field finders lose to earlier same-shaped text (CNH field 3 'SAO PAULO/SP' beat field 4c 'SSP/SP'). Anchor dependent fields to their parent value's position (019849fe: issuer adjacent to the RG number). Also: CNH prints RG without check digit (13032360) while the RG card/contract carry it (13.032.360-3) — true to document, not a bug; a later RG-card upload should be allowed to enrich, not conflict.

The refresher reads the PRIMARY checkout's project-history/auto-improvement.ndjson even when run from a worktree (and even with REPO_ROOT=<worktree>), while the pre-commit gate all-cache-freshness-auto-improvement hashes the WORKTREE's ledger. The cache is shared (.git/noctusai/cache/). Whenever the primary lags origin/dev (e.g. it cannot fast-forward because of untracked files), every worktree commit is blocked: the gate says stale and the refresher says in-sync / rebuilds from the wrong ledger. Seen 2026-09-21: primary=418668880970, worktree=79cbd4109849. Fix: resolve the ledger from the invoking tree, the same way the gate does.

Dispatching an engineer with Agent isolation='worktree' AND a brief telling it to task_branch start: the harness pins the agent's git sandbox to its own agent-* worktree, so it can write files into the task_branch worktree but can never git add/commit there. The backend engineer finished its work (343 tests green) but the tech-lead had to commit it. Rule: use one or the other, never both (task_branch briefs should run without harness isolation). Related improvement: noctus.dev.salvage_worktree could take stage_all / paths so a sandboxed caller can finish end to end.

Product frontends are never type-checked in CI: product-frontend-tests runs vitest and a few jobs run `vite build`, neither of which type-checks, and seed-typecheck.yml covers only seed/*. Live 2026-09-21: the manual-address slice added 6 required ImovelDados fields; ImovelCartorioCard.test.tsx's fixture lacked them; vitest 1723 green + vite build green, `tsc --noEmit` red — merged to dev unnoticed. Fix: add `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` per product in the product-frontend-tests matrix (scoped by the new changes job), after first measuring which products currently fail tsc (fix those, don't gate blind).

Order-dependent tests surface the moment a suite is sharded: 3 MCP tests passed only because an earlier file ran first (sys.path added by a sibling test file; `import server` inside a test strips caplog's root handler via configure_logging). Rule: shared path setup lives in conftest; import modules with import-time side effects (logging config) at collection time, never inside a test. Fixed abf7711f.

Process slip (tech-lead, 2026-09-21): pushed the seed Sidebar change to dev without waiting for its CI; ERP sidebar E2E (which encodes the old expanded-by-default contract) went red and dev stayed red across ~6 subsequent pushes (all cancelled by concurrency, so nobody saw a completed red). A UX-contract change in a shared organ must be pushed and its CI watched to completion before stacking more pushes; E2E specs that encode the old contract are part of the change.

check_framework_deps(fix=True) writes "*" as the version range for missing organ deps (donor lookup found nothing for react-markdown/remark-gfm/rehype-slug even though seed/lib/frontend/package.json declares ^10.1.0/^4.0.1/^6.0.0) and re-serialises every touched package.json with 4-space indent (whole-file churn). Worked around on 2026-09-23 by adding the deps by hand with the seed lib's ranges (commit f02fe0550). Fix: donor = seed lib's own package.json first; preserve the file's detected indent. Also: the CLI's --fix only applies with --predeploy-check, so --check-framework-deps has no CLI fix path.

wire_env hazard: `npm install` inside a wire_env'd worktree (per-package node_modules symlinked into the PRIMARY) wrote through the shared scoped-package folder and broke the primary's products/core/frontend vitest resolution (`Cannot find package '@vitest/utils'`); the engineer repaired it with `npm install` in primary. Safe recipe used for lockfile regen: `npm install --package-lock-only` (never touches node_modules). Fix: document --package-lock-only in self-branching-mode §5a for dependency changes and/or have wire_env refuse or warn when node_modules is a symlink and npm install is run.

Primary checkout found on 2026-09-23 with an unresolved `git pull --autostash` conflict (stash@{0} 'autostash' from 2026-09-22 00:47, UU on mcp/noctusai/catalog.md + Sidebar.organ.yaml — derived artifacts; stash side semantically a stale subset) plus a local-only branch-pointer commit, which made branch_pointer pushes fail with dirty_blocked. Resolved by sanctioned `git reset --hard origin/dev` after saving the ledger diff; the lost pointer row was re-recorded. The stash entry was left in place (shared stash stack). Root cause is unknown: some pull path uses --autostash on dev with regenerable artifacts dirty. Fix: whichever tool pulls in primary should never autostash derived artifacts (regenerate instead).

MarkdownRenderer seed organ landed 2026-09-23 (consumer #1: core Website → Documentação). Migration candidates: knowledge-extractor/frontend/src/pages/Methodology.tsx (whitespace-pre-wrap) and academia-de-reciclagem/frontend/src/components/MarkdownBlock.tsx (product-local markdown renderer, making this N=2 → triage). Also: register_organ failed with OpenAI 429 (credits exhausted), so the organ's .organ.yaml isn't indexed into code-embeddings; re-run after credits are restored.

A branch_pointer ledger-only commit in the PRIMARY (only project-history/branch-tree{,.mirror}.ndjson staged) ran pre-commit's `cli.py --check-eight-way-sync --worktree-path <primary>` at 100% CPU for more than 6.5 minutes. description: Live extraction probe 2026-09-21 (Anthropic vision, image-only 3-page certidão de casamento) returned rg_orgao='COTIA/SP' for a document that contains NO RG at all. The fixture's only nearby text is "LOCAL: Cotia - SP"; the parser took the place name as an issuing organ and emitted a field the source never asserted, while leaving `rg` itself null — so the pair is internally incoherent (an orgão expedidor with no document number). Everything else on that read was exact: cpf 285.660.330-00, data_casamento 2010-03-14, data_emissao 2024-06-06, estado_civil 'divorciado' (correctly read off the page-3 averbação), regime_bens 'comunhao_parcial'. Two things worth fixing: (1) rg_orgao should never be emitted without an rg — an orphan orgão is evidence the parser matched geography, not an ID; (2) `nacionalidade` and `profissao` are present in the fixture's page 1 and were NOT extracted, and both are hard-required by the contract's qualification gate, so the operator still has to type them by hand even on a perfect read. This matters beyond tidiness: contract §5.2's whole premise is that extracted values are the truth, and a fabricated qualification field goes into a legal instrument.

A hand-created lead has no contract surface for up to 6 hours and an operator cannot speed it up. Verified live 2026-09-21: created a lead through the UI (/leads → Base de Leads → Novo lead) with a valid contato_norm. The funil auto-created its atendimento immediately — titulo='+5511988770001' (the phone, since the dialog cannot capture a name) — but with cliente_id NULL. Per the card-hub's own routing, a card with cliente_id NULL opens LeadDetailModal, not ClienteCardDialog, so there is NO Contratos subpage, no Negociação, no document intake: the entire contract pipeline is unreachable. cliente_id is attached only by clientes_backfill_job, whose interval defaults to 6h (config.clientes_backfill_interval_hours=6). There is a startup catch-up (added 2026-08-31 for exactly this class of starvation) but it only helps leads that existed BEFORE the restart. POST /api/clientes/backfill exists on the router but has no operator-facing surface anywhere in the UI — no button on /clientes, /clientes/revisao or the funil. The module's own docstring already names the consequence ("unmovable, because stage_gate refuses a card with no titular") for the scheduler-starvation case; this is the same dead end reached by simply creating a lead by hand. Worth either attaching the cliente synchronously on manual lead creation (the contato_norm is right there and fully resolvable) or exposing the existing backfill route as an operator action.

description: When the MCP server is stale, task_branch integrate falls back to a fresh subprocess, and that fallback crashes: `_default_run_local` runs `git status` with cwd=wt_path, where wt_path is the RELATIVE '.claude/worktrees/<slug>'. The subprocess's cwd is not the repo root, so it raises FileNotFoundError, and the result is reported as 'fresh_subprocess_outcome_unknown' even though nothing ran. Workaround used: run `python mcp/noctusai/cli.py --task-branch=integrate ...` from the repo root. Fix: resolve wt_path against LEDGER_ROOT/REPO_ROOT (absolute) before any subprocess, and/or launch the fresh subprocess with cwd=repo root.

False alarm, 2026-11-10 04:32Z, session 5ff8685d: the hook reported "59 background agent(s) of THIS session handed back but are still held" and listed 8 ids. TaskStop on each of the 8 (plus 3 more that finished tonight) returned "No task found"; the harness reports only 1 running agent. The hook derives "held" from its own ledger of hand-backs and never reconciles it against the harness's live task list, so it nags the leader to stop agents that no longer exist. That costs a turn and trains leaders to ignore the warning. Fix: reconcile against live tasks before warning, or drop an entry once TaskStop says "No task found" or a final task-notification arrives. Destination: tooling queue (hooks), same owner as e1's tooling steward lane.

description:
EOA append-only event tables are guarded by row-level BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers. Row triggers never fire on TRUNCATE (PostgreSQL CREATE TRIGGER docs), and service_role usually holds GRANT ALL. So any holder of a product's service-role key (every product container) can wipe or forge the "immutable" history.
On origin/dev about 81 migrations mention append-only guards; only 5 carry a BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger.
Found by the adversarial security pass on core 118 (fixed there, before apply).
Build triad:
- construction: scaffold_migration / the seed append-only helper emits a BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT raise, plus SELECT-only grants and a SECURITY DEFINER writer;
- backstop: a keeper flags an append-only table without a TRUNCATE guard, warn-first with a ratchet baseline;
- telemetry: verify_db_guards gains truncate_refused probes.
Fan-out: per-product migrations, pilots first, each prod apply with the owner's go.
Destination: tooling-engineer for the keeper and scaffold; architect to check EOA KB wording.

TRUST-BOUNDARY finding (security advisor, S1 re-check round 3, 2026-11-10): the transcript-based owner-consent verification, which prod_consent uses and which S1 reused for personal lines, can be forged and replayed. Transcripts under ~/.claude/projects are ordinary user-writable files, and an agent with the Write tool can append to them (agents already write memory under that tree). The lookup accepts any session id on the machine, in any project. There is no time window, no single-use nonce, no binding to the executing session, and a fuzzy intent-match fallback is accepted. Impact: the rule "prod consent = the owner's typed phrase in the session that runs the deploy" holds by convention, not by construction. Proposed fix, for an OWNER DECISION: out-of-band confirmation (a one-time code sent through noctus.dev.notify to the owner's own channel), bound to action, plan hash, expiry and nonce, exact match only. Same root as the invocation-context design seed ('authority.owner_consent valid only when bound to the same root and session'). Destinations: the go_live council's blocker questions tonight; the owner questions list; project-history/roadmaps/invocation-context-2026-11.md. Not fixed tonight, because the consent mechanism is the owner's to design. Interim in S1: personal-line provisioning is refused outright.

Hypothesis held. A non-lease session delivered steward tooling end to end through the guardian's queue, LINEAR. Guardian touches = 0 (b5 only enqueued). Ejections = 0: it landed first try (cc19031f9, run 42785416134), within one working night (claim ~04:25Z → landed ~09:05Z). The role works as specified, so this is not discard. It is not plain adopt, because 6 friction points surfaced, each with a concrete refinement:
(1) branch_pointer had no steward role (fixed in-branch).
(2) Peer scope-adds arrived by message and grew the brief mid-flight. Absorbing them worked, but a stewarded branch needs a live scope list.
(3) The adversarial loop was decisive: pass 1 found 2 P1 that 639 green tests missed.
(4) Dogfooding the contract on its own delivery found what both review passes missed: run_scoped never ran on the real repo. Rule: every preflight item gets a "green on current dev HEAD" test.
(5) The steward's own verdict-channel and shell slips. A piped rc, and zsh not word-splitting: two wrong diagnoses before the real cause. Use a bash runner script, and name the interpreter before diagnosing.
(6) A hook-changing delivery needs a primary FF right after landing, or the old guard still governs. Rebased-twin branches absorbed by cherry-pick are invisible to `landed` and need `cleanup`.

description:
[surprise] The breaker went through 3 build rounds, each green on deliverable and on red-first tests. The 3rd security pass still found 3 P1s:
- Julia's worker runs under the inherited `startup` source, so outside traffic can silence it.
- Request-path work and the audit flush run as `unattributed`, so anonymous POSTs can trip them and blind the audit.
- The CLI bypasses the steward gate.
It also found that the credit scheme defeats the budget (P2).
Two of the P1s and both P2s share one root cause: the design holds sources it cannot reliably attribute. Patching each finding would not fix that. The fix is a redesign: only named, owned loops can be held, catch-alls are alert-only, and per-job caps replace credits.
Lesson: when review rounds keep finding new holes in the same control, step back to first principles rather than patch again.
